docs.title: Competitive Intelligence — Docs Home
docs.text: Welcome to the engineering and operations documentation for the Competitive Intelligence Aggregator — a FastAPI + LLM application that watches competitor sources, extracts and scores business signals, and delivers the results to analysts through an admin panel, weekly digests, and alerts. These docs are for the internal engineers who extend the system and the operators who run scans and review intelligence.

docs.title: What this tool is
docs.text:
The Aggregator continuously monitors competitor websites, news, careers pages, blogs, and social channels, then turns what it finds into ranked, explained intelligence about your competitive landscape. It runs as three cooperating layers:

Scan → Intelligence → Delivery. Layer 1 scans each configured source and emits CandidateSignal rows; Layer 2 clusters, classifies, scores, and impact-assesses those signals into DetectedChange deliverables; Layer 3 assembles and sends weekly digests and high-significance alerts.

The pipeline is grounded in Godrej Consumer Products (GCP) as the home company, tracking competitors such as HUL, P&G India, ITC, Marico, Dabur, and Reckitt.

docs.title: Architecture at a glance
docs.text:
The diagram below is the whole system on one screen. The full, annotated version and per-layer diagrams live in System Architecture.

flowchart TB
    subgraph Control["Control plane"]
        YAML[Competitor YAML] --> Loader[yaml_loader]
        Panel[Admin panel<br/>/admin/panel] --> Routers[7 FastAPI routers]
        Loader --> DB[(Database<br/>SQLite / Azure SQL)]
        Routers --> DB
    end

    Sched[Scheduler<br/>get_due_sources] --> Queue[[Queue<br/>InMemory / Service Bus]]
    Queue --> Worker[SourceScanWorker]

    subgraph L1["Layer 1 — Scanning"]
        Worker --> Adapters[Source adapters]
        Adapters --> Blob[(Blob store<br/>local / Azure)]
        Adapters --> Analyzers[Analyzers + cheap gate]
        Analyzers --> CS[CandidateSignal]
    end

    subgraph L2["Layer 2 — Intelligence"]
        CS --> Orch[Core Intelligence<br/>Orchestrator]
        Orch --> DC[DetectedChange]
        Orch --> Alert[AlertCandidate]
        Orch --> Digest[DigestEntryDraft]
    end

    subgraph L3["Layer 3 — Delivery"]
        DC --> Assembler[DigestAssembler]
        Assembler --> Email[Email]
        Assembler --> Teams[Teams]
    end

    LLM[LLM provider<br/>Mock / Azure OpenAI]
    LLM -.-> Analyzers
    LLM -.-> Orch
    Orch -.telemetry.-> DB
    LLM -.cost.-> DB

    Control --> Sched

docs.title: Choose your path
docs.text:
• Get Started — install, configure, and run your first scan, report, and feedback loop end-to-end.
  • Concepts & Architecture — the mental model: three layers, the data model, scoring, the feedback governance system, and all the diagrams.
  • Reference — dry facts: CLI commands, REST endpoints, config keys, and the data model.
  • Admin Panel Guide — how to drive the single-file admin panel screen by screen.
  • Operations & Runbook — deploy, monitor, back up, and troubleshoot in production.

docs.title: Key facts
docs.text:
• Language / framework: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Typer CLI.
  • Storage: SQLite locally, Azure SQL in production; blobs on local disk or Azure Blob.
  • LLM: Azure OpenAI (gpt-4o) in production, a deterministic mock provider offline. One structured-JSON interface (complete_json).
  • Admin panel: a single scripts/admin_panel.html, no build step, served at /admin/panel.
  • CLI: ci-agent <cmd> (equivalent to python -m app.cli <cmd>).
  • Infra abstractions: queue, blob store, and LLM provider are swapped between local and Azure by the ENVIRONMENT setting and connection strings.

Note

In server mode the app only enqueues scan jobs — it does not run an always-on worker. Jobs execute via the CLI (dev-run-once, worker-once, run-pipeline) or a separate Service Bus consumer in production. See System Architecture.

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text: This page tracks the version history of the Competitive Intelligence Aggregator, what is currently implemented, the known gaps, and — importantly — the corrections between the older in-repo developer notes (CLAUDE.md / README.md) and the actual code. Where the two disagree, the code (as documented in this site) wins.

docs.title: Current version
docs.text: v0.1.0 — competitive-intel, requires-python >= 3.11. Stack: FastAPI + Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic, httpx / BeautifulSoup / lxml / feedparser, Typer CLI (ci-agent), Azure OpenAI client, Playwright, Azure Service Bus + Blob SDKs, Apify client.

docs.title: What's done
docs.text:
• Layer 1 — scanning: all adapters (website, careers, news, blog/social) and all analyzers with LLM integration, behind a cheap deterministic gate.
  • Layer 2 — intelligence: the full 15-step pipeline (normalize → cluster → classify → score → assess) producing DetectedChange plus delivery drafts and cumulative competitor profiles.
  • LLM: AzureOpenAIProvider (gpt-4o via Azure OpenAI) and a deterministic MockLLMProvider for offline tests; single complete_json interface.
  • News: Tavily provider (plus Bing/Brave/Mock auto-detect).
  • Server & UI: FastAPI server with the full single-file admin panel at /admin/panel.
  • Observability: AgentRunTelemetry per-agent metrics, cost ledger, and the Gantt/timeline view.
  • Standalone agents: structured I/O metadata on all agents (the standalone-tool pattern).
  • Feedback: suppression UI to mark signals as noise, plus the governance pipeline (proposals, policy packs, eval harness).

docs.title: Known gaps / remaining TODOs
docs.text:
• Azure Service Bus queue — AzureServiceBusSourceScanQueue exists; production wiring/rollout of the separate consumer process is not fully operationalized.
  • Azure Blob store — AzureBlobStore exists; production adoption pending.
  • Alembic migrations — only partially adopted; schema is still mainly create_all + _safe_add_columns (see below and Backup & Migrations).
  • ATS connectors — Greenhouse/Lever/Workday connectors are present but the Workday path falls back to generic HTML; ATS-specific coverage is incomplete.
  • Layer 3 — delivery — digest assembly, email, and Teams exist; broader alert dispatch/scheduling hardening remains.
  • Brave Search provider — available as an alternative to Tavily (BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY) but less exercised.

docs.title: Documentation corrections vs CLAUDE.md / README.md
docs.text:
The following corrections consolidate drift found across the source material. The older CLAUDE.md and README.md are wrong on these points; this site reflects the real code.

Topic Older docs say (incorrect) Actual code Analyzer package app/analyzers/ (flat <type>_analyzer.py, app/analyzers/registry.py) app/analysis/ with per-type packages (app/analysis/<type>/analyzer.py, app/analysis/registry.py) Adapter package flat app/adapters/<type>_adapter.py per-type packages app/adapters/<type>/adapter.py Observability routes app/api/observability_routes.py app/admin/observability_routes.py — there is no app/api/ directory; every router lives under app/admin/ Worker in server mode implies scans run automatically the server only enqueues; nothing consumes the queue automatically — a worker (worker-once / dev-run-once) or a separate Service Bus consumer must run. The server-side scheduler starts only the WeeklyDigestScheduler Startup hook (unstated) startup uses the deprecated FastAPI on_event hook, not lifespan — a known migration item Config loading (unstated) load-config has no dedup — re-running duplicates competitors and sources

See Add a New Source Type for the correct extension paths and Deployment for the worker/startup behavior.

docs.title: v0.1.0 — initial release
docs.text:
• Layer 1 scanning: adapters + analyzers + cheap gate + scan worker + scheduling/queueing.
  • Layer 2 intelligence: 15-step orchestrator, deterministic-first clustering with LLM merge judge, deterministic significance scoring, LLM impact assessment grounded in Godrej Consumer Products (competitors HUL, P&G India, ITC, Marico, Dabur, Reckitt).
  • Layer 3 delivery: weekly digest assembler, email (permissive SSL, skipped when SMTP_HOST unset), Teams cards.
  • Feedback & governance: two suppression subsystems, proposal lifecycle, policy-pack compilation with token budgets, evaluation harness.
  • Observability: telemetry hierarchy, cost ledger (USD + INR at rate 85), pipeline board, live run, timeline, incidents + maintenance actions, Copilot.
  • Azure-ready abstractions for queue, blob, LLM, and database selected at runtime by ENVIRONMENT + connection strings.
  • Single-file admin panel (scripts/admin_panel.html) served at /admin/panel; ci-agent CLI.

docs.title: Admin Control Plane
docs.text: The Admin Control group is where operators manage the system's configuration and inspect its audit trail: competitors and their sources, per-source schedules, the scan console, run history, news profiles (with full versioning), and the audit log. These screens perform soft-deleting CRUD over the control-plane tables and record every mutation to AdminAuditLog (with before/after/diff and originating IP).

docs.title: Admin Competitors & Sources
docs.text:
Screens: admin-competitors (loader loadAdminCompetitors), admin-sources (loader loadAdminSources)

CRUD over competitors and their sources. Competitors: POST /admin/competitors (201), GET /admin/competitors?active_only, GET /admin/competitors/{id}, PATCH /admin/competitors/{id}, DELETE /admin/competitors/{id} (204). Sources can be created nested under a competitor (POST /admin/competitors/{id}/sources) or flat (POST /admin/sources, which requires a competitor_id), and listed via GET /admin/sources?competitor_id.

Deletes are soft

DELETE on a competitor or source deactivates the row (deactivate_competitor) rather than removing it. Filter with active_only / is_active to hide deactivated rows.

See Add a Competitor & Sources.

docs.title: Schedules
docs.text:
Screen: admin-schedules · loader loadAdminSchedules

Manages one SourceSchedule per source. Endpoints: GET /admin/sources/{id}/schedule (404 if none), POST /admin/sources/{id}/schedule (201; 409 if a schedule already exists; computes next_run_at and audits), PATCH /admin/sources/{id}/schedule (recomputes and audits), DELETE /admin/sources/{id}/schedule (204), and GET /admin/schedules?enabled_only.

A schedule's schedule_type is one of manual | hourly | daily | weekly | cron. Cron schedules use a cron_expression evaluated with croniter; the next run is computed by _compute_next_run.

30-minute minimum frequency

Guardrails cap how aggressively a source can be scanned: MIN_FREQUENCY_MINUTES = 30, MAX_QUERY_BUDGET = 20, MAX_PAGES = 50, MAX_CONCURRENT_SCANS = 10. A schedule cannot run more often than every 30 minutes.

docs.title: Scan Console
docs.text:
Screen: admin-scan-console · loader loadAdminScanConsole

The manual scan trigger — six request types, background submission (202), and run polling. This screen has its own deep-dive: see the Manual Run Console.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Screen: admin-runs · loader loadAdminRuns

The run list with a jobs drill-down. It lists runs (GET /admin/runs?limit&status), shows a single run (GET /admin/runs/{id}), and drills into per-source job detail (GET /admin/runs/{id}/jobs — SourceScanLog rows with resolved source/competitor names, status, attempt count, error_type/error_message, and candidate_signals_count). Use it to review what a run did and where it failed.

docs.title: News Profiles
docs.text:
Screen: admin-news-profiles · loader loadAdminNewsProfiles

The news-profile editor with full versioning, rollback, and two dry-run tools. Core endpoints: GET /admin/news-profiles, GET /admin/competitors/{id}/news-profile (404), POST (201; 409 if one exists; records v1 + audit), PATCH (updates, snapshots a version, audits the diff), and DELETE (204 + audit).

  • Versioning & rollback — GET .../news-profile/versions?limit=20 lists snapshots; POST .../news-profile/rollback/{version_id} applies a snapshot and records a new version with is_rollback = true plus an audit entry.
  • Preview queries — GET .../news-profile/preview-queries?budget=10 returns the queries the profile would generate (build_queries_from_profile, falling back to build_queries) without running a scan.
  • Test relevance — POST .../news-profile/test-relevance { title, snippet, url } returns { decision: pass | suppress | llm_review, reasons }, running the active profile's profile_relevance_check (or fast_relevance_check if no profile is active).

See Configure a News Profile.

docs.title: Audit Log
docs.text:
Screen: admin-audit-log · loader loadAdminAuditLog

The full mutation history from AdminAuditLog, via GET /admin/audit-logs?object_type&object_id&limit=100. Every control-plane change — competitor, source, schedule, or news-profile edit — writes a before/after/diff record with the originating IP. Use it to answer "who changed what, and when."

docs.text:

  • Configure a News Profile — versioning and relevance tuning.
  • API — Schedules & News Profiles — endpoint reference for these screens.

docs.title: Feedback & Governance Screens
docs.text:
These screens are the control room for how the system learns. They cover the Feedback & Tuning group (scoring weights, agent configs, legacy suppressions) and the Governance group (natural-language commands, the proposal review queue, mined patterns, the rule library, the weights editor, policy packs, policy health, and live runtime state). Together they let an operator inspect what feedback has produced, approve or reject proposed policy changes, compile and activate policy packs, and see exactly which rules are gating live runs.

The governance pipeline is deterministic

Feature extraction, pattern mining, and proposal generation use no LLM — proposal text comes from templates. The only LLM-backed screens here are NL-Command, and the consolidation feature inside Policy Health. See Feedback & Learning Governance.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Screen: scoring (Feedback & Tuning) · loader loadScoringWeights

Lists scoring-weight profiles and lets you create, activate, and patch them. Backing endpoints: GET /admin/scoring-weights, POST /admin/scoring-weights (creates, no auto-activate), PUT /admin/scoring-weights/{id}/activate, PATCH /admin/scoring-weights/{id} (merges weight_updates), and GET /admin/scoring-weights/defaults. Exactly one profile is active at a time. See Tune Scoring Weights.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Screen: agents (Feedback & Tuning) · loader loadAgentConfigs

Manages per-agent prompt addenda and feedback. It lists agent configs (GET /admin/agent-configs, GET /admin/agent-configs/{agent_name}), lets you append feedback (POST /admin/agent-configs/{agent_name}/feedback, with feedback_type one of instruction | correction | example | constraint), and reset an agent (DELETE /admin/agent-configs/{agent_name}/reset).

docs.title: Suppressions
docs.text:
Screen: suppressions (Feedback & Tuning) · loader loadSuppressions

Manages the legacy FeedbackSuppressionEntry table (Layer 1 suppression), via GET/POST/DELETE /admin/feedback/suppressions.

Two suppression systems, not unified

This screen manages legacy FeedbackSuppressionEntry rows only. Governance SuppressionRule rows (Layer 2) are created by approving proposals and appear under the Rule Library and Runtime State. The two tables are separate. See Manage Suppressions.

docs.title: NL-Command
docs.text:
Screen: nl-command (Governance) · loader (LLM parser)

A free-text command box that parses a natural-language instruction into a structured governance action and executes it. It posts to POST /admin/feedback/nl-command (LLM). Parsed actions include add_rule, suppress, adjust_weight, compile_pack, deactivate_rule, and query.

docs.title: Governance (proposals)
docs.text:
Screen: governance (Governance) · loader loadProposals

The human-review queue — the heart of governance. It lists pending FeedbackChangeProposal records (with a red badge for the pending count) and lets you approve or reject each one:

  • GET /admin/feedback/proposals?status&limit
  • POST /admin/feedback/proposals/{id}/approve (optionally with edited_change_json)
  • POST /admin/feedback/proposals/{id}/reject

Approval always activates the proposal regardless of its risk_level. What activation does depends on the proposal type: a suppression_rule becomes an active SuppressionRule; a scoring_weight_change deactivates the current profile and inserts a new active ScoringWeightProfile; an agent_policy_rule creates an active AgentPolicyRule and auto-recompiles that agent's default pack. See Review & Approve Feedback Proposals.

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text:
Screen: patterns (Governance) · loader loadPatterns

Read-only view of mined FeedbackPattern records (GET /admin/feedback/patterns). Each pattern is keyed by error type / agent / failure-mode / category / source-type, with a computed frequency and severity. Patterns are what drive proposal generation once they cross frequency thresholds.

docs.title: Rule Library
docs.text:
Screen: rule-library (Governance) · loader loadRuleLibrary

CRUD over AgentPolicyRule records, backed by GET /admin/feedback/agent-policy-rules, GET /admin/feedback/agent-policy-rules/all?agent_name&status, POST, and PATCH /{id}. This is where the raw policy rules live before they are compiled into packs.

docs.title: Weights Editor
docs.text:
Screen: weights-editor (Governance) · loader loadWeightsEditor

Governance-side view of scoring weight profiles via GET /admin/feedback/weight-profiles/active and POST /admin/feedback/weight-profiles. Complements the Feedback & Tuning Scoring screen with the governance profile lineage.

docs.title: Policy Packs
docs.text:
Screen: policy-packs (Governance) · loader loadPolicyPacks (+ loadPolicyRules, loadEvalCases)

The compile/activate/edit workbench, plus evaluation. Backing endpoints:

  • GET /admin/feedback/policy-packs?agent_name — list packs
  • POST /admin/feedback/policy-packs/compile — compile (3 modes: custom_text, rule_ids, all-active)
  • PATCH /admin/feedback/policy-packs/{id} and POST /admin/feedback/policy-packs/{id}/activate
  • Eval cases: POST /admin/feedback/eval-cases (201), GET ?agent_name, POST /admin/feedback/eval-cases/{id}/approve, and POST /admin/feedback/eval-runs

Pack budgets

A pack must fit within 400 tokens and 8 rules and contain no duplicates, or activate is blocked. Per-run budget across packs is 800 tokens. See Compile & Activate Policy Packs and Run the Evaluation Harness.

docs.title: Policy Health
docs.text:
Screen: policy-health (Governance) · loader loadPolicyHealth

The budget and coverage cockpit, backed by /admin/policy-health/*: GET /admin/policy-health?agent_name (pack + latest snapshot), GET /admin/policy-health/{id} (recomputes and persists a snapshot), POST /admin/policy-health/{id}/consolidate (LLM merge/retire/convert → PolicyConsolidationProposal), GET/PATCH on consolidation proposals, GET /admin/policy-health/{id}/coverage-map, and POST /admin/policy-health/simulate (combined-budget simulation). Use it to spot near-budget or over-budget packs, duplicate rules, and coverage gaps.

docs.title: Runtime State
docs.text:
Screen: runtime-state (Governance) · loader loadRuntimeState

The live view of everything currently gating runs — active rules, packs, weight profiles, and suppressions — via GET /admin/feedback/runtime-state. Check this after approving proposals to confirm the change is actually in force.

docs.text:

  • Compile & Activate Policy Packs — pack budgets and activation gates.
  • API — Feedback Governance & Policy Health — endpoint reference.

docs.title: Intelligence Screens
docs.text: These screens are where operators read the system's output: the daily dashboard, pipeline health, the detected-changes feed (with impact drill-down and the feedback form), the LLM query box, competitor profiles, and the weekly digest and delivery logs. They span three of the panel's navigation groups — Overview, Intelligence, and Delivery — and are all read-first, with a few key actions (submit feedback, ask a question, assemble and send a digest).

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Screen: dashboard (Overview) · loader loadDashboard

The landing screen. It shows KPI tiles summarising the current state of the pipeline and offers quick actions wired directly to the API:

  • Run Layer 2 → POST /admin/run-layer2
  • Clean up scan runs → POST /admin/scan-runs/cleanup (marks stuck running runs as abandoned)
  • Assemble & send weekly digest → POST /admin/weekly-digests/assemble-and-send

Use it as your at-a-glance health check and as a shortcut for the most common one-click operations.

docs.title: Pipeline Health
docs.text:
Screen: pipeline-health (Overview) · loader loadHealth

Displays pipeline health metrics over a rolling window, backed by GET /admin/pipeline-health?n_days=7. Read this to confirm recent runs are producing changes at the expected rate before you dig into individual runs on the observability screens.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
Screen: changes (Intelligence) · loader loadChanges

The core intelligence feed. It lists DetectedChange records and lets you filter by competitor, significance, and status via GET /admin/detected-changes?competitor&significance&status&limit. Selecting a change drills into its full detail — including the impact assessment and feedback history — through GET /admin/detected-changes/{id}.

Each change detail carries a feedback form. Submitting it posts an analyst verdict:

POST /admin/detected-changes/{id}/feedback

Allowed verdicts are correct, false_positive, low_priority, over_rated, under_rated, needs_reanalysis, and missed (an invalid verdict returns 422). This single form is the entry point to the entire feedback and governance system.

Feedback drives two subsystems

A verdict flows into both the legacy/immediate path (which may archive the change or reset signals right away) and the governance path (which mines patterns and generates human-review-gated proposals). See Feedback & Learning Governance.

docs.title: Query
docs.text:
Screen: query (Intelligence) · loader (LLM Q&A)

A natural-language question box over the competitor profiles. It posts to the LLM-backed endpoint:

POST /admin/query   { "question": "...", "competitor": "..." }

The backend runs a QueryService that answers from the accumulated CompetitorProfile data. Use it for ad-hoc questions ("what has HUL been doing in premium detergents?") without hand-filtering the changes feed.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
Screen: profiles (Intelligence) · loader loadProfiles

Shows each competitor's cumulative CompetitorProfile alongside its recent detected changes, backed by GET /admin/profiles and GET /admin/profiles/{competitor_id}. Profiles are the long-memory view of a competitor; the changes feed is the event stream.

docs.title: Digests
docs.text:
Screen: digests (Delivery) · loader loadDigests

Manage WeeklyDigest objects — assemble, preview, and send. Backing endpoints:

  • GET /admin/weekly-digests?limit=20 — list digests
  • POST /admin/weekly-digests/assemble — assemble a new digest (201)
  • POST /admin/weekly-digests/assemble-and-send — assemble and deliver in one step
  • POST /admin/weekly-digests/{id}/send — send to {recipients}
  • GET /admin/weekly-digests/{id}/html — preview the rendered HTML

Email delivery is conditional

Sending is skipped when SMTP_HOST is unset, and the mail path uses permissive SSL by design for the corporate proxy. See Assemble & Send a Weekly Digest.

docs.title: Delivery Logs
docs.text:
Screen: delivery-logs (Delivery) · loader loadDeliveryLogs

A record of what was actually sent, via GET /admin/delivery-logs?limit=50. Check this after a send to confirm delivery and to diagnose recipients that did not receive a digest or alert.

docs.text:
• Governance Screens — act on the feedback you submit here.
  • Assemble & Send a Weekly Digest — the full delivery workflow.
  • API — Intelligence & Delivery — endpoint reference for these screens.

docs.title: Manual Run Console
docs.text: The Manual Run Console (admin-scan-console, loader loadAdminScanConsole) is the panel's cockpit for triggering scans on demand. From one form you choose one of six request types, the console builds the right parameters, submits the request, and then polls until the run finishes. This page walks through opening the console, the six request types and their parameter builders, what happens after you submit, and how to watch the run to completion.

docs.title: Opening the console
docs.text: Select Admin Control → Scan Console in the left rail. The form presents a request-type selector; the JavaScript shows or hides the extra inputs (a competitor picker, a source-ID field) depending on the type you choose, assembles a params_json object, and posts it.

docs.title: The 6 request types and their param builders
docs.text:
All six are handled server-side in _run_scan_in_background. The console builds params_json per type:

Request type What it does params_json all_sources Enqueue every active source (schedule_scan(None)) {} competitor_sources Enqueue all active sources for one competitor { "competitor_id": ... } single_source Enqueue one source { "source_id": ... } layer2_only Run the Layer 2 orchestrator only, skipping the queue { "scan_run_id"?, "competitor_id"?, "limit"? } retry_failed Re-enqueue the failed SourceScanLog rows of a prior run { "scan_run_id": ... } rebaseline Clear last_scan_at, then enqueue { "source_id": ... }

The console shows the competitor picker for competitor_sources and the source-ID field for single_source and rebaseline.

layer2_only bypasses the queue

Queue-based types (all_sources, competitor_sources, single_source, retry_failed, rebaseline) enqueue jobs via schedule_scan and need a worker to consume the queue. layer2_only instead calls the CoreIntelligenceOrchestrator.run directly and does not touch the queue.

docs.title: Submitting and status transitions
docs.text:
Submitting posts to the scan-request endpoint, which accepts the work immediately and returns 202:

POST /admin/scan-requests
{ "request_type": "...", "params_json": { ... }, "requested_by": "admin" }

The response is a ScanRequestOut with status = "created". The background task then advances the request through its lifecycle:

created → running → completed   (with scan_run_id)
                 → failed        (with error_message)

The server only enqueues

Except for layer2_only, submitting a request enqueues jobs but does not execute them. A worker (CLI worker-once, or a Service Bus consumer in production) must be running for queued jobs to actually run. See Run a Manual Scan.

docs.title: Watching the run
docs.text:
After submitting, the console polls GET /admin/scan-requests?limit=20 to track the request itself. The Live Run and Scan Runs views poll the run-visibility endpoints:

  • GET /admin/runs/current — the latest running (or most recent) run, with total/completed/failed job counts
  • GET /admin/runs/{id} — a specific run
  • GET /admin/runs/{id}/jobs — the per-source SourceScanLog rows, each resolved with source name/type, competitor name, status, timestamps, adapter name, attempt count, error_type, error_message, and candidate_signals_count

The jobs view is where you diagnose a partially failed run — see Recover a Failed Run.

docs.title: D17 — Manual run lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as Console (UI)
    participant API as scan_request_routes
    participant BG as BackgroundTasks
    participant ORCH as Orchestrator / Queue
    participant DB as DB

    UI->>API: POST /admin/scan-requests
    API-->>UI: 202 ScanRequestOut (status=created)
    API->>BG: _run_scan_in_background
    BG->>DB: status = running
    alt layer2_only
        BG->>ORCH: CoreIntelligenceOrchestrator.run (skip queue)
    else queue types
        BG->>ORCH: schedule_scan (enqueue jobs)
    end
    ORCH-->>BG: result
    BG->>DB: status = completed (+scan_run_id) / failed (+error_message)
    loop poll
        UI->>API: GET /admin/scan-requests?limit=20
        UI->>API: GET /admin/runs/{id}/jobs
        API-->>UI: status + per-source job rows
    end

docs.title: Observability Screens
docs.text:
The Observability group is the operator's telemetry suite: nine screens for watching runs live, checking system and source health, drilling into completed runs, tracking LLM usage and cost, managing incidents, asking an ops copilot for help, exploring the cost ledger, and monitoring agent load. Every screen is backed by /admin/observability/* in app/admin/observability_routes.py, which reads the telemetry hierarchy (PipelineRun → CompetitorRun → AgentRunTelemetry → LLMCostLedger, plus CurrentRunState). Costs are shown in both USD and INR (USD_TO_INR = 85).

The workflow:stage key format is load-bearing

The pipeline board keys stages as workflow:stage:agent_name and per-competitor statuses as workflow:stage, ordered by STAGE_ORDER. The panel's JavaScript parses these keys directly to render the board. Never change the key format — doing so silently breaks the Live Run and Runs boards.

docs.title: Live Run
docs.text:
Screen: obs-live-run · loader loadLiveRun

A live flowchart of the currently executing run, with a LIVE badge. It polls GET /admin/observability/pipeline-board and GET /admin/observability/runs/current on an interval to animate stage-by-stage progress. GET /runs/current returns a CurrentRunState: stage, agent, competitor, progress %, elapsed time, sources/signals done vs total, cost, and the list of active_agents. This is the screen to keep open while a scan or pipeline is running.

docs.title: Obs Health
docs.text:
Screen: obs-health · loader loadObsHealth

The system health overview, backed by GET /admin/observability/system-health (aggregated in observability/health_aggregator.py). Start here to answer "is the system OK right now?"

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Screen: obs-runs · loader loadObsRuns

The completed-run explorer. It lists pipeline runs (GET /admin/observability/pipeline-runs?limit=20), drills into one (GET /admin/observability/pipeline-runs/{id}, including per-SourceScanLog detail), renders the pipeline board for that run (GET /admin/observability/pipeline-board?pipeline_run_id&scan_run_id), and shows a timeline / Gantt view (GET /admin/observability/runs/{id}/timeline) of AgentRunTelemetry laid out by start time with a per-competitor summary.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Screen: obs-sources · loader loadObsSources

Per-source health, via GET /admin/observability/source-health?status&competitor. Use it to find sources that are consistently failing or returning nothing.

docs.title: LLM
docs.text:
Screen: obs-llm · loader loadObsLlm

LLM metrics and per-run cost. Backed by GET /admin/observability/llm-metrics?hours=24 and GET /admin/observability/llm-runs?hours=720 (per-PipelineRun cost, sourced primarily from LLMCostLedger with an LLMTrace fallback; the response's data_source field says which). Read this to attribute spend to specific runs.

docs.title: Incidents
docs.text:
Screen: obs-incidents · loader loadObsIncidents

Incident tracking plus maintenance actions. Incidents: GET /admin/observability/incidents?status&limit=50, POST (create, defaulting severity="sev2"), and PATCH /{id} (update status/severity/root-cause/blast-radius/component; setting status to resolved auto-stamps resolved_at). Maintenance actions follow an approval lifecycle: GET /admin/observability/maintenance-actions, POST (creates as pending_approval), PATCH /{id} (approve → records approved_by; execute → stamps executed_at + result_json). See Incident Response.

docs.title: Copilot
docs.text:
Screen: obs-copilot · loader loadCopilotActions

An LLM ops assistant with an action queue, via POST /admin/observability/copilot. It is given live context — system health, current runs, the last 6 hours of LLM metrics, problem sources, and open incidents — and can auto-create MaintenanceAction rows: risky actions land as pending_approval, safe ones as approved.

docs.title: Costs
docs.text:
Screen: obs-costs · loader loadCostExplorer

The cost explorer over the LLM cost ledger, grouped on demand: GET /admin/observability/costs?group_by=agent|competitor|run|source&hours=24 (an unrecognised group_by returns 400). Costs roll up AgentRunTelemetry → CompetitorRun → PipelineRun and are reported in USD and INR.

docs.title: Agent Load
docs.text:
Screen: obs-agent-load · loader loadAgentLoad

Per-agent load and performance, via GET /admin/observability/agents/load?hours=24: run counts, latency (p95 computed in Python), error and success rates, cost, the agents active now, and totals. Use it to find slow or expensive agents.

docs.title: Panel Overview & Navigation
docs.text: The admin panel is the operator's cockpit for the Competitive Intelligence Aggregator. It is a single, self-contained HTML file served by the FastAPI app that surfaces every part of the system — dashboards, the intelligence feed, feedback and governance tooling, deep observability, and the admin control plane — across 32 screens grouped into 7 functional areas. This page explains how the panel is served, the design system it uses, the full screen map, the frontend patterns every screen shares, and how a click travels all the way to the database.

docs.title: What the panel is
docs.text:
The entire panel is one file, scripts/admin_panel.html (~371 KB, ~6000 lines), with all CSS and JavaScript inline. There is no build step — no bundler, no framework, no npm install. The FastAPI app reads the file at request time and returns it as an HTMLResponse:

# app/main.py:36-38
@app.get("/admin/panel")
def admin_panel():
    return HTMLResponse(_PANEL_HTML.read_text(...))

Open it in a browser once the server is running:

http://localhost:8000/admin/panel

The app is titled "Competitive Intelligence Aggregator" (v0.1.0) and mounts seven routers, each backing one theme of the panel:

Router variable File URL theme router app/admin/routes.py /health, competitors, sources, scan-runs intelligence_router app/admin/intelligence_routes.py scoring, agents, changes, query, digests, feedback governance observability_router app/admin/observability_routes.py /admin/observability/* policy_health_router app/admin/policy_health_routes.py /admin/policy-health/* schedule_router app/admin/schedule_routes.py source schedules scan_request_router app/admin/scan_request_routes.py manual scan requests, run visibility, audit logs news_profile_router app/admin/news_profile_routes.py news profiles + versioning

All routers live under app/admin/

There is no app/api/ directory. In particular, the observability endpoints live in app/admin/observability_routes.py, not app/api/.

docs.title: Design system
docs.text:
The panel uses its own slate-dark palette defined in CSS variables:

--dark:  #0d1117;   /* page background      */
--mid:   #161b22;   /* raised surfaces      */
--panel: #21262d;   /* cards / panels       */
--border:#30363d;   /* dividers             */
--text:  #e6edf3;   /* primary text         */

Categorical accents for charts, chips, and per-competitor colour coding come from COMP_COLORS:

COMP_COLORS = ['#58a6ff','#3fb950','#f78166','#d29922','#c084fc','#38d9a9','#ff9e7b'];

The panel theme is not the Godrej brand

This dark developer theme is an internal operator tool and is deliberately distinct from the organisation's black-and-white brand system. Do not treat the panel palette as brand guidance; it exists purely for at-a-glance readability of dense operational data.

docs.title: The 7 groups and 32 screens
docs.text:
Navigation is a left rail. Selecting an item calls navigate(sec), which toggles the active section and invokes that screen's loader. The groups and their screens:

Each group maps to the deep-dive pages in this section: Intelligence Screens, Governance Screens, Observability Screens, the Manual Run Console, and the Admin Control Plane.

docs.title: Frontend patterns
docs.text:
Every screen is built from a handful of shared helpers, so learning one screen teaches you all of them.

  • apiFetch(path, opts) — the single HTTP helper. It prepends apiBase(), sets the JSON Content-Type, stringifies non-string bodies, throws Error("<status>: <text>") on any non-OK response, and returns parsed JSON (or text). A known fix ensures it does not double-stringify a body that is already a string.
  • sections / sectionLoaders / navigate(sec) — sections maps each screen name to its DOM container; sectionLoaders maps each screen name to its data-loading function. navigate(sec) toggles .nav-item.active / .section.active on #section-<sec>, sets #page-title, and calls sectionLoaders[sec](). This is the entire routing model.
  • statusChip(s) and badge helpers — statusChip, badgeSig, badgeStatus, badgeActive, adminAlert, and showAlert render coloured status pills and inline alerts from a status string via CSS variables.
  • No authentication — the panel sends no auth headers, and the API uses permissive CORS (*).

No authentication — trusted network only

The panel and its API have no login and open CORS. This is safe only on a trusted internal network. Never expose /admin/panel or the API to the public internet.

Costs throughout the panel are shown in both USD and INR (the ledger applies a fixed USD_TO_INR = 85 conversion).

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text: When you interact with a screen, the click reaches the database along one of three paths: a plain read/write through a router and the repositories layer; an LLM-backed endpoint that calls build_llm_provider().complete_json; or a scan request that is accepted immediately (202) and executed in the background.

docs.title: D15 — Request flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    UI["Panel screen<br/>admin_panel.html"] --> AF["apiFetch(path)"]
    AF --> R["FastAPI router<br/>app/admin/*.py"]
    R --> V["Pydantic schema<br/>+ repositories.py"]
    V --> DB[("SQLite / Azure SQL")]

    R -->|LLM endpoints| LLM["build_llm_provider()<br/>.complete_json"]
    LLM --> DB

    R -->|scan requests| BG["BackgroundTasks<br/>_run_scan_in_background"]
    BG --> Q["Queue"]
    Q --> W["Worker"]
    W --> TC["observe_agent →<br/>AgentRunTelemetry / LLMCostLedger"]
    TC --> DB

The startup sequence (app/main.py:46-69) prepares this flow: it runs create_all, starts the scheduler, seeds the LLMPriceCatalog, wires the DB session factory into the LLM provider for the cost ledger, and marks any orphaned running PipelineRun / ScanRun / AgentRunTelemetry rows as interrupted. The server also shares a single InMemorySourceScanQueue via set_queue and set_scan_request_queue.

docs.title: Data Model & Lineage
docs.text: This page shows how data flows and relates across the system — from configuration rows through Layer 1 artifacts, into the Layer 2 intelligence chain, and out to delivery. It concentrates on the relationships and lineage; for a dry, table-by-table column and enum listing, see Data Model & Enums.

docs.title: Entity groups
docs.text:
The models (app/db/models.py, ~1374 lines; UUID string primary keys, JSON columns suffixed _json) fall into groups:

  • Layer 1 — Competitor, Source, ScanRun, SourceScanLog, RawArtifact, NormalizedDocument, DocumentBlock, SourceItem, LowLevelDelta, ChangePackage, LLMTrace, CandidateSignal.
  • Layer 2 — CandidateSignalArchive, EvidenceBundle, NormalizedSignal, AtomicClaim, EventCluster, EventClusterSignalLink, EventEvidence, FinalClassification, SignificanceScore, ImpactAssessment, DetectedChange, AlertCandidate, DigestEntryDraft, ProfilePatch, HistoricalIndexDocument, ReasoningTrace, CompetitorProfile.
  • Scoring / delivery / feedback / observability / control plane — ScoringWeightProfile, WeeklyDigest, DeliveryLog, the governance tables, PipelineRun/CompetitorRun/AgentRunTelemetry/LLMCostLedger, and SourceSchedule/ScanRequest/CompetitorNewsProfile/AdminAuditLog.

docs.title: The lineage chain
docs.text:
Each CandidateSignal fans out through evidence and normalization into a shared EventCluster, which accumulates one classification, score, and impact assessment before producing the central DetectedChange deliverable. From there, delivery artifacts and the cumulative CompetitorProfile are derived.

erDiagram
  Competitor ||--o{ Source : has
  Competitor ||--o{ EventCluster : owns
  Competitor ||--|| CompetitorProfile : "cumulative"
  Source ||--o{ ScanRun : "scanned in"
  Source ||--o{ SourceItem : discovers
  Source ||--o{ CandidateSignal : produces
  CandidateSignal ||--|| EvidenceBundle : hydrates
  CandidateSignal ||--o| NormalizedSignal : normalizes
  NormalizedSignal ||--o{ AtomicClaim : "splits into"
  AtomicClaim }o--|| EventCluster : "clusters by fingerprint"
  EventCluster ||--o{ EventClusterSignalLink : links
  EventCluster ||--o{ EventEvidence : cites
  EventCluster ||--|| FinalClassification : classified
  EventCluster ||--|| SignificanceScore : scored
  EventCluster ||--|| ImpactAssessment : assessed
  EventCluster ||--|| DetectedChange : yields
  DetectedChange ||--o| AlertCandidate : "may alert"
  DetectedChange ||--o| DigestEntryDraft : "may digest"
  DetectedChange ||--o{ ProfilePatch : patches
  DetectedChange ||--o| HistoricalIndexDocument : indexes
  ProfilePatch }o--|| CompetitorProfile : "applied to"

  CandidateSignal {
    string id PK
    string status "candidate / promoted_to_layer_2"
    string dedup_fingerprint
    float confidence
  }
  EventCluster {
    string id PK
    string event_fingerprint UK "competitor+action+entity+cat"
    string status "classified / scored / detected_change_created"
    int source_count
  }
  SignificanceScore {

    string current_status "active / disappeared"

docs.title: Key uniqueness and identity
docs.text:
• SourceItem — unique on (source_id, fingerprint); the fingerprint is required and set by the adapter.
  • NormalizedDocument.content_hash — drives change detection between scans.
  • EventCluster — unique index ix_event_clusters_competitor_fingerprint on (competitor_id, event_fingerprint); this is what makes clustering deterministic-first.
  • EventClusterSignalLink — unique on (cluster_id, candidate_signal_id), created under a savepoint guard.
  • CompetitorProfile — one row per competitor (profile_json), updated in place by applied ProfilePatches.

docs.title: Config → data flow
docs.text:
Configuration becomes rows in two ways: the .env file and per-source YAML config blocks drive the runtime factories (via Settings and app/infra.py), while the competitor YAML is loaded into Competitor and Source rows. From there the scan and pipeline populate the full lineage chain.

flowchart TD

  YAMLCFG["per-source config blocks"] -.overrides.-> SET
  SET --> INFRA["infra.build_queue / build_blob_store / build_llm_provider"]

  YAMLC["competitor YAML"] --> LOAD["yaml_loader.load_config_from_yaml"]
  LOAD --> COMP["Competitor"]
  LOAD --> SRC["Source"]

  COMP --> SR["ScanRun"]
  SRC --> SR
  SR --> SSL["SourceScanLog"]
  SRC --> RA["RawArtifact"]
  RA --> ND["NormalizedDocument"]
  ND --> DB2["DocumentBlock"]
  DB2 --> LLD["LowLevelDelta"]
  LLD --> CP["ChangePackage"]
  CP --> CSIG["CandidateSignal"]
  CSIG --> EB["EvidenceBundle"]
  EB --> NS["NormalizedSignal"]
  NS --> AC["AtomicClaim"]
  AC --> EC["EventCluster"]
  EC --> FC["FinalClassification"]
  FC --> SS["SignificanceScore"]
  SS --> IA["ImpactAssessment"]
  IA --> DC["DetectedChange"]
  DC --> ALT["AlertCandidate"]
  DC --> DED["DigestEntryDraft"]

load-config never de-duplicates

load_config_from_yaml always inserts — it has no upsert or dedup. Re-running it against the same YAML creates duplicate Competitor and Source rows. See How-to: Add a Competitor & Sources.

YAML config overrides .env

A per-source config block takes precedence over the corresponding .env setting. This lets one source use a different news provider or crawl budget than the global default.

docs.title: Feedback & Learning Governance
docs.text:
When an analyst reviews a DetectedChange and says "false positive," "over-scored," or "mis-classified," the system captures that verdict and turns recurring mistakes into governed policy changes. This page explains the two feedback subsystems, the governance lifecycle, the proposal state machine, and how approved rules compile into policy packs that gate future runs.

The governance pipeline has NO LLM

Feature extraction, pattern mining, and proposal generation are 100% deterministic (rule text comes from templates). The LLM appears only in three narrow places: the legacy scoring-weight decision, policy consolidation (POST /admin/policy-health/{id}/consolidate), and eval runs that exercise LLM agents.

docs.title: Two subsystems
docs.text:
Both are invoked from POST /admin/detected-changes/{change_id}/feedback, and they maintain two parallel, non-unified suppression tables.

Subsystem Location Role Suppression table Legacy / immediate app/intelligence/feedback.py, agent_feedback.py, scoring_weights.py Immediately mutates state: archives changes, resets signals, creates suppressions, LLM-adjusts weights FeedbackSuppressionEntry (Layer 1) Governance (main) app/feedback/ (~15 files) Deterministically mines feedback into patterns and proposals that need human approval before any policy change SuppressionRule (Layer 2)

The two suppression systems are not unified

FeedbackSuppressionEntry is enforced in Layer 1 (the scan worker and news analyzer); SuppressionRule is enforced in Layer 2 (the orchestrator). Creating one does not create the other. See How-to: Manage Suppressions.

docs.title: The feedback loop
docs.text:
The verdict flows down both paths at once: the legacy path applies some effects immediately, while the governance path mines the feedback into human-review-gated proposals that, once approved, become active policy and improve future runs.

flowchart TD
  classDef llm fill:#efe,stroke:#3fb950,color:#111
  V["Analyst verdict"] --> POST["POST /detected-changes/{id}/feedback"]
  POST --> AF["submit_feedback → AnalystFeedback"]

  AF --> LEG["Legacy: apply_feedback"]
  LEG --> L1["archive change / reset signals"]
  LEG --> L2["FeedbackSuppressionEntry"]
  LEG --> L3["LLM weight adjust"]:::llm

  AF --> GOV["Governance: FeedbackService"]
  GOV --> FE["FeatureExtractor"]
  FE --> PM["PatternMiner (freq, severity)"]
  PM --> PG["ProposalGenerator"]
  PG --> PR["FeedbackChangeProposal<br/>pending_human_review"]
  PR --> APP{approve?}
  APP -->|yes| ACT["_activate_proposal"]
  ACT --> R1["SuppressionRule"]
  ACT --> R2["new ScoringWeightProfile"]
  ACT --> R3["AgentPolicyRule → compile_pack"]
  R1 --> GATE["Runtime gating<br/>L1 / L2 / scoring"]
  R2 --> GATE
  R3 --> GATE
  GATE -.improves.-> V

docs.title: The governance lifecycle
docs.text:
FeedbackService.process_feedback() (app/feedback/service.py) orchestrates stages 3–6 in a try/except with rollback, then sets feedback.status to proposal_created (if proposals were generated) or structurally_applied.

  1. Capture — submit_feedback() writes AnalystFeedback (received, applied=False).
  2. Feature extraction — FeedbackFeatureExtractor.extract() → FeedbackFeature.
  3. Pattern mining — FeedbackPatternMiner.mine() → FeedbackPattern.
  4. Immediate structural actions — archive / URL suppression.
  5. Proposal generation — ProposalGenerator.generate_from_feedback() → FeedbackChangeProposal.
  6. Review & approval — HumanReviewService.approve_proposal() / reject_proposal() → _activate_proposal().
  7. Policy compilation — PolicyCompiler.compile_pack() / activate_pack() → CompiledPolicyPack.
  8. Runtime application & gating — assemble_runtime_bundle(), SuppressionService, SourceReliabilityService.
  9. Regression testing — EvaluationCaseService.run_eval() → EvaluationRun.

docs.title: Verdicts and effects
docs.text:
The HTTP layer allows seven verdicts. They differ in what the legacy path applies immediately versus what the governance path proposes.

Verdict Legacy immediate Governance LLM weight adj false_positive archive (archived_fp), FeedbackSuppressionEntry per URL suppression_rule proposal (every occurrence) + agent_policy_rule (freq ≥ 2) Yes over_rated → over_scored none scoring_weight_change (freq ≥ 2) + agent_policy_rule (freq ≥ 2) Yes under_rated → under_scored none same, weight increase Yes needs_reanalysis resets promoted signals to candidate, marks change needs_reanalysis none No low_priority note only none No correct note only none No missed not handled by legacy error_type false_negative, no proposal builder matches Yes

docs.title: Feature extraction and pattern mining
docs.text: Feature extraction is fully deterministic: it derives error_type, failure_mode, market_scope, source_authority, publisher domain, and various boolean features. Pattern mining upserts a FeedbackPattern keyed on _build_pattern_key (error_type | agent | mode | cat | src), recomputes frequency, and assigns severity — for the high-severity set (false_positive, false_negative, over_scored, misclassified, wrong_geography): freq ≥ 5 critical, ≥ 2 high, else medium.

docs.title: Proposal types and thresholds
docs.text:
ProposalGenerator has three builders with a threshold of 2:

  • suppression_rule — on false_positive, not frequency-gated (every occurrence). Values are one source URL per URL from the change (up to 5), else the event fingerprint.
  • scoring_weight_change — on over_scored/under_scored with freq ≥ 2 and a category present; magnitude ±10%.
  • agent_policy_rule — on a set of error types with freq ≥ 2; the target agent is chosen by error type (agent_for_error), ignoring the feedback's own agent name.

Dual proposals on over/under-scored

An over_scored or under_scored pattern at freq ≥ 2 produces both a scoring_weight_change and an agent_policy_rule, both targeting the scorer. This is intentional — the two mechanisms are independent.

docs.title: Proposal state machine
docs.text:
Approval always activates. Three related state machines govern proposals, compiled packs, and consolidation proposals.

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> pending_human_review
  pending_human_review --> approved: approve
  pending_human_review --> edited_and_approved: approve + edits
  pending_human_review --> rejected: reject
  approved --> [*]: _activate_proposal
  edited_and_approved --> [*]: _activate_proposal
  rejected --> [*]

  state "CompiledPolicyPack" as Pack {
    [*] --> draft
    [*] --> budget_exceeded
    draft --> active: activate_pack
    active --> superseded: newer pack
  }

  state "PolicyConsolidationProposal" as Cons {
    [*] --> pending_review
    pending_review --> approved_c: approve
    pending_review --> rejected_c: reject
    approved_c --> applied: recompile + retire
  }

Approval always activates

approve_proposal sets should_activate=True regardless of the proposal's risk_level; the human-approval flags only gate auto-activation, not the manual approval action itself.

docs.title: Policy compilation and token budgets
docs.text:
Approving an agent_policy_rule creates an active AgentPolicyRule and auto-recompiles the agent's default pack. compile_pack() (app/feedback/policy_compiler.py) loads active rules by priority, takes the first 8, numbers them into compiled_text, and estimates tokens at 1.3 per word. If the estimate exceeds 400 the pack is budget_exceeded, otherwise draft. It supersedes the prior active pack for the same (agent_name, pack_name) and writes a PolicyPackHealthSnapshot and PolicyCoverageMap.

flowchart TD
  A["approve agent_policy_rule"] --> B["AgentPolicyRule active"]
  B --> C["compile_pack"]
  C --> D["load rules by priority, cap 8"]
  D --> E["compiled_text + token estimate (1.3/word)"]
  E --> F{tokens > 400?}
  F -->|yes| G["status budget_exceeded"]
  F -->|no| H["status draft"]
  H --> I["supersede prior active"]
  I --> J["snapshot + coverage map"]
  J --> K["activate_pack"]
  K --> L{gate: ≤400 tokens, ≤8 rules, no dupes}
  L -->|pass| M["status active + fresh snapshot"]
  L -->|fail| N["ValueError — blocked"]

Budget constants

Per-pack budget is 400 tokens with a maximum of 8 rules; the per-run budget across up to 5 packs is 800 tokens. activate_pack raises ValueError and blocks if any of those limits (or duplicate detection) fails.

docs.title: Runtime gating
docs.text: At runtime, assemble_runtime_bundle() (app/feedback/prompts.py) uses the PolicyStore and RuleApplicabilityEngine to select applicable rules by structural scope matching (every scope key must equal the corresponding context field; empty = global), sorts by specificity then priority, enforces the 800-token prompt budget, and appends rules between --- ACTIVE POLICIES --- markers. Suppression (SuppressionService), source reliability (SourceReliabilityService), and admin-authored HardRules also gate at runtime.

docs.title: Evaluation harness
docs.text: EvaluationCaseService.run_eval() runs active EvaluationCases against a policy pack and writes an EvaluationRun. The scoring agent runs deterministically; LLM agents (classification, impact, news relevance) call the real system prompt plus addendum; others are skipped. Comparison tolerances: bool exact, float ±0.2, int ±10%, list subset, string case-insensitive. See How-to: Run the Evaluation Harness.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• Two suppression systems (FeedbackSuppressionEntry in L1, SuppressionRule in L2) — not unified.
  • agent_policy_rule retargets by error type and ignores the feedback's own agent_name.
  • eval_case, prompt_version_change, and poor_impact_analysis appear in coverage maps but have no active emitter (planned/partial).

docs.title: Item Lifecycle & Status
docs.text: The key entities in the pipeline carry a status that records where they are in their life. This page walks the status transitions of the main items — SourceItem, CandidateSignal, EventCluster, and DetectedChange — across both layers, and explains how feedback can reset an item for reprocessing.

docs.title: SourceItem status
docs.text: A SourceItem (a discovered page, article, job posting, or post) is active while it keeps appearing in scans. When a scan no longer finds it, mark_items_disappeared flips it to disappeared. This transition is itself a signal source (for example, a closed job posting).

docs.title: CandidateSignal status
docs.text: A CandidateSignal starts as candidate from Layer 1. Layer 2 intake and quality routing move it onward: valid, promotable signals become promoted_to_layer_2 once they join a cluster; noise is suppressed_source_noise; invalid signals are archived; and signals that fail validation land in needs_review.

docs.title: EventCluster status
docs.text: An EventCluster advances through the cluster-level pipeline steps: it is created, then classified (step 9), scored (step 10), and finally detected_change_created (step 12) once its DetectedChange exists.

docs.title: DetectedChange status
docs.text: A DetectedChange is ready when its band is High/Medium/Low, or archived when the band is Archive. Feedback can move it to archived_fp (false positive) or needs_reanalysis (see below).

docs.title: The combined lifecycle
docs.text:
The three intelligence entities progress in lockstep: a promoted signal joins a cluster, the cluster is classified/scored/finalized, and the resulting change is either delivered or archived. Feedback can pull a change back into reprocessing.

stateDiagram-v2
  state "CandidateSignal" as CS {
    [*] --> candidate
    candidate --> promoted_to_layer_2: quality route promote
    candidate --> suppressed_source_noise: suppress
    candidate --> archived_cs: archive_only
    candidate --> needs_review: intake invalid
    promoted_to_layer_2 --> candidate: needs_reanalysis feedback
  }

  state "EventCluster" as EC {
    [*] --> created
    created --> classified: step 9
    classified --> scored: step 10
    scored --> detected_change_created: step 12
  }

  state "DetectedChange" as DC {
    [*] --> ready: band High/Medium/Low
    [*] --> archived: band Archive
    ready --> archived_fp: false_positive feedback
    ready --> needs_reanalysis: needs_reanalysis feedback
    needs_reanalysis --> ready: reprocessed
  }

  CS --> EC: joins cluster
  EC --> DC: yields change

docs.title: Run status
docs.text:
The run-tracking entities have their own lifecycles:

  • ScanRun — created, then rolled up to completed / degraded / failed; POST /admin/scan-runs/cleanup moves stuck running runs to abandoned.
  • PipelineRun — spans Layer 1 + Layer 2 + delivery; completed, or failed only when there are failures and zero changes.
  • ScanRequest — created → running → completed / failed.
  • CompiledPolicyPack — draft / budget_exceeded → active → superseded (see Feedback & Learning Governance).

Orphan cleanup on startup

On startup the server marks any PipelineRun, ScanRun, or AgentRunTelemetry left in running state (from a crash or restart) as interrupted, so the observability screens do not show phantom live runs.

docs.title: How feedback resets status
docs.text: The needs_reanalysis verdict is the one that reaches back into an earlier stage: the legacy feedback path resets the change's promoted CandidateSignals from promoted_to_layer_2 back to candidate and marks the DetectedChange needs_reanalysis, so the next Layer 2 run reprocesses them from scratch. See Feedback & Learning Governance.

docs.text:

docs.title: Layer 1 — Source Scanning
docs.text: Layer 1 is the ingestion and first-pass extraction stage. For each due Source, a source-type-specific adapter fetches raw data, the worker persists it, and a matching analyzer diffs it against the previous scan and applies a cheap deterministic gate (with optional LLM assistance) to produce CandidateSignal rows — the input to Layer 2. This page explains the adapter and analyzer patterns, the scan worker, and how work is scheduled and queued.

docs.title: Purpose and role
docs.text: The unit of work is a Source (a website page, a website crawl scope, a news search, a careers page, a blog/RSS feed, or a social channel) belonging to a Competitor. The output is CandidateSignal rows with status candidate. The orchestration boundary is SourceScanWorker.process_job().

docs.title: Layer 1 end-to-end
docs.text:
The path from a due source to a persisted candidate signal is deterministic-first: cheap checks run before any LLM call, and the first scan of a source only establishes a baseline.

flowchart TD
  classDef llm fill:#efe,stroke:#3fb950,color:#111
  A["schedule_scan"] --> B["get_due_sources"]
  B --> C["create SourceScanLog<br/>+ SourceScanJob"]
  C --> D["Queue.enqueue"]
  D --> E["SourceScanWorker.process_job"]
  E --> F["AdapterRegistry<br/>resolve by source_type"]
  F --> G["Adapter.scan → AdapterScanResult"]
  G --> H["persist raw artifacts → BlobStore"]
  H --> I["persist normalized docs + blocks"]
  I --> J["upsert source items"]
  J --> K["AnalyzerRegistry<br/>resolve by source_type"]
  K --> L["Analyzer.analyze"]
  L --> M{cheap gate}
  M -->|suppress_noise| N["drop / note"]
  M -->|candidate_without_llm| P["CandidateSignal draft"]
  M -->|llm_review| Q["LLM prompt"]:::llm
  Q --> P
  P --> R["persist_analysis_result"]
  R --> S[("DB: CandidateSignal")]
  S --> T["Layer 2"]

docs.title: The adapter pattern
docs.text:
The contract is app/adapters/base.py: SourceAdapter.scan(source, competitor, context) -> AdapterScanResult. Adapters are stateless — configuration comes from source.config_json plus get_settings(). Every adapter returns an AdapterScanResult (app/schemas/adapter.py) carrying fetched_artifacts, normalized_documents, and discovered_items (each item requires a fingerprint).

The registry (app/adapters/registry.py) maps source types to adapters:

Source type Adapter File website_page, website_scope WebsiteAdapter app/adapters/website/adapter.py news_search NewsSearchAdapter app/adapters/news/adapter.py careers CareersAdapter app/adapters/careers/adapter.py blog, social BlogSocialAdapter app/adapters/blog_social/adapter.py

Behavior differs by type: website_page does a single GET; website_scope does a depth-1 BFS crawl honoring POLITENESS_DELAY_SECONDS; news_search runs search-provider queries (no page fetch); careers detects the ATS and dispatches to a connector; blog parses RSS or an HTML index; social dispatches to LinkedIn/Twitter providers or deterministic mock posts.

Adapters do no LLM work

Adapters only fetch and normalize. All LLM assistance happens in the analyzer stage. All adapter HTTP uses httpx with verify=False (deliberate, corporate proxy).

docs.title: Connectors and providers (adapter dispatch)
docs.text:
Within an adapter, a second dispatch chooses the concrete connector or provider. For news and social the choice is by configured provider or auto-detection (search providers skip keys that start with PASTE); for careers it is by ATS detection with a Playwright fallback.

flowchart TD
  ST{source_type}
  ST --> WEB["website_page / website_scope<br/>WebsiteAdapter"]

  ST --> NEWS["news_search<br/>NewsSearchAdapter"]
  NEWS --> N1["Bing"]
  NEWS --> N2["Tavily"]
  NEWS --> N3["Brave"]
  NEWS --> N4["Mock"]

  ST --> CAR["careers<br/>CareersAdapter"]
  CAR --> C1["Greenhouse"]
  CAR --> C2["Lever"]
  CAR --> C3["Workday → generic HTML"]
  CAR --> C4["Generic HTML + Playwright fallback"]

  ST --> BLG["blog<br/>BlogSocialAdapter"]
  BLG --> B1["RSS / Atom parse"]
  BLG --> B2["HTML index parse"]

  ST --> SOC["social<br/>BlogSocialAdapter"]
  SOC --> S1["LinkedIn (Apify)"]
  SOC --> S2["Twitter (Apify)"]
  SOC --> S3["mock posts"]

News provider auto-detect priority is Bing → Tavily → Brave → Mock. A missing social key produces a warning, not a failure.

docs.title: The analyzer pattern
docs.text:
The contract is app/analysis/contracts.py: SourceAnalyzer.analyze(source, competitor, scan_run, adapter_result, persisted_scan_objects, repositories, llm_provider) -> SourceAnalysisResult. The registry (app/analysis/registry.py) mirrors the adapter registry by source type.

Every analyzer follows the same shape: fetch previous state via repository lambdas → detect deltas (the first scan emits only a baseline_created delta and no signals) → run the cheap gate (app/analysis/cheap_gate.py, returning no_action / suppress_noise / llm_review / candidate_without_llm) → on llm_review call the LLM → build a CandidateSignalDraft.

First scan is baseline only

Because change detection diffs against a prior scan, the very first scan of a source records a baseline and produces no candidate signals. Signals appear from the second scan onward.

docs.title: The scan worker flow
docs.text:
SourceScanWorker.process_job() (app/workers/source_scan_worker.py) runs a 12-step sequence. The adapter and analyzer each run inside their own observe_agent() telemetry span, and error handling is asymmetric: pre-flight failures retry, while adapter/analyzer runtime failures acknowledge without retry.

sequenceDiagram
  participant Q as Queue
  participant W as SourceScanWorker
  participant AD as Adapter
  participant DB as DB / BlobStore
  participant AN as Analyzer
  participant LLM as LLMProvider
  Q->>W: receive(job)
  W->>DB: load source + competitor
  alt missing source/competitor
    W->>DB: mark_scan_log_failed(NotFound)
    W->>Q: ack
  else resolved
    W->>DB: mark_scan_log_running
    Note over W,AD: observe_agent(adapter, layer1, source_type)
    W->>AD: scan()
    alt adapter raises
      W->>DB: _fail_job (mark failed)
      W->>Q: retry
    else success
      AD-->>W: AdapterScanResult
      W->>DB: persist raw / docs / items
      Note over W,AN: observe_agent(analyzer, source_type_analyze)
      W->>AN: analyze()
      AN->>LLM: complete_json (only on llm_review)
      LLM-->>AN: LLMResult (or error_message)
      AN-->>W: SourceAnalysisResult
      W->>DB: persist_analysis_result
      W->>DB: mark_scan_log_success + counts
      W->>Q: ack
    end
  end

Retry acknowledgement asymmetry

_fail_job marks the log failed and calls queue.retry, which increments the attempt count and dead-letters after MAX_QUEUE_ATTEMPTS (default 3). But adapter/analyzer runtime failures ack the message (no retry) — only pre-flight failures (for example a missing adapter registration) retry. LLM failures never crash the pipeline; the provider returns an LLMResult with error_message and empty output_json. See Error Handling, Retries & Status Codes.

docs.title: Scheduling and queueing
docs.text:
SourceSchedule holds one row per source (schedule_type manual/hourly/daily/weekly/cron, next_run_at indexed). get_due_sources() (app/scheduler/due_sources.py) selects schedules whose next_run_at is in the past, adds the source, and immediately advances next_run_at to prevent double-enqueue. schedule_scan() (app/scheduler/service.py) then creates a ScanRun, a SourceScanLog and SourceScanJob per source, and enqueues each job.

The queue itself is chosen by app/infra.build_queue(): InMemorySourceScanQueue (a deque, used by the server) or AzureServiceBusSourceScanQueue (production, lock-token ack/abandon/dead-letter). Both dead-letter a job after MAX_QUEUE_ATTEMPTS.

docs.title: LLM assistance points
docs.text:
LLM use in Layer 1 is analysis-only and always conditional on a gate decision. Each analyzer owns its prompts:

Prompt (v1) Analyzer Purpose website_semantic_diff Website meaningful positioning shift vs noise careers_role_normalizer Careers classify job title → function careers_pattern_interpreter Careers hiring surge / geo expansion → signal news_relevance_resolver News is a borderline article about this competitor news_event_extractor News extract business event + signal_type blog_social_post_interpreter BlogSocial interpret a post → signal

docs.title: Extension points
docs.text: To add a source type you write an adapter package, an analyzer package, and register the type string in both registries. See the walkthrough in How-to: Add a New Source Type.

docs.text:

docs.title: Layer 2 — Intelligence Pipeline
docs.text:
Layer 2 is the multi-step pipeline that converts raw CandidateSignal rows from Layer 1 into deduplicated, classified, scored, and impact-assessed DetectedChange records — plus delivery artifacts and a cumulative CompetitorProfile. This page explains the 15-step orchestrator, which steps use the LLM, and how deduplication and clustering work.

Grounded in Godrej Consumer Products

Every LLM prompt in this pipeline is written for Godrej Consumer Products (GCP) as the home company; the monitored competitors are HUL, P&G India, ITC, Marico, Dabur, and Reckitt. The impact_analysis prompt (v2) hardcodes GCP brand, category, and market lists plus grounding rules. This is the app's internal domain framing — distinct from the documentation site's branding.

docs.title: Purpose and role
docs.text: The input is CandidateSignal rows with status candidate or promoted_to_layer_2_pending. The output chain is: CandidateSignal → NormalizedSignal → EventCluster → FinalClassification → SignificanceScore → ImpactAssessment → DetectedChange, followed by delivery preparation, profile patching, and historical indexing. The code lives in app/intelligence/ (roughly 21 files).

docs.title: The orchestrator
docs.text:
CoreIntelligenceOrchestrator (app/intelligence/orchestrator.py) is constructed with a Session and an optional LLM provider, and lazily loads the single active ScoringWeightProfile. The entry point is:

process_candidate_signals(candidate_signal_ids=None, scan_run_id=None, limit=100, pipeline_run_id=None) -> CoreIntelligenceRunResult

It loads signals, creates or attaches a PipelineRun, groups signals by competitor_id (one CompetitorRun each), and processes each signal through _process_one (steps 1–8). It commits after every signal to release the SQLite write lock between LLM calls; a failed signal is rolled back individually and recorded in result.failures. The returned CoreIntelligenceRunResult carries counters for everything created (normalized signals, clusters, detected changes, alerts, digest entries, profile patches, LLM calls, failures).

docs.title: The full pipeline
docs.text:
Steps 1–8 (_process_one) run per signal; steps 9–15 (_process_cluster) run once the signal has joined a cluster. Five steps can invoke the LLM (marked in green); the rest are deterministic. Three decision points can short-circuit the flow.

flowchart TD
  classDef llm fill:#efe,stroke:#3fb950,color:#111

  subgraph SL["Signal-level — _process_one (1-8)"]
    S1["1 Intake validation"] --> V{valid?}
    V -->|no| ARC1["archive → needs_review"]
    V -->|yes| S2["2 Load competitor + source"]
    S2 --> S3["3 Evidence hydration"]
    S3 --> S4["4 Normalization"]:::llm
    S4 --> S5{5 Quality routing}
    S5 -->|suppress / archive_only| STOP["stop"]
    S5 -->|promote| S6["6 Atomic claims"]
    S6 --> S7["7 Fingerprinting"]
    S7 --> S8["8 Clustering"]:::llm
  end

  S8 --> S9

  subgraph CL["Cluster-level — _process_cluster (9-15)"]
    S9["9 Final classification"]:::llm --> S10["10 Significance scoring"]
    S10 --> BAND{band}
    BAND -->|Archive| ARC2["DetectedChange status archived"]
    BAND -->|High / Medium / Low| S11["11 Impact assessment"]:::llm
    S11 --> S12["12 DetectedChange upsert"]
    S12 --> S13["13 Delivery preparation"]
    S13 --> S14["14 Profile patch + narrative"]:::llm
    S14 --> S15["15 Historical index"]
  end

docs.title: Signal-level steps (1–8)
docs.text:
# Step File / function LLM? 1 Intake validation intake.py validate_candidate() No 2 Load related inline (Competitor + Source) No 3 Evidence hydration evidence.py build_evidence_bundle() No 4 Signal normalization normalization.py normalize_signal() Yes (conditional) 5 Quality routing quality_router.py route_signal() No 6 Atomic claims atomic_claims.py build_atomic_claims() No 7 Fingerprinting fingerprinting.py build_fingerprint() No 8 Clustering clustering.py find_or_create_cluster() Yes (conditional merge judge)

Intake checks status, evidence, IDs, non-blank title/summary/type, and confidence ≥ 0.25; invalid signals are archived with status needs_review. Evidence hydration classifies source authority (official → first_party → reputable_news → third_party_news → social → careers → weak_snippet → unknown). Normalization does a deterministic first pass and only calls the LLM when needs_llm(). Quality routing promotes on official/reputable + confidence ≥ 0.45, high-value category + confidence ≥ 0.45, or confidence ≥ 0.55; suppress/archive_only short-circuits.

docs.title: Cluster-level steps (9–15)
docs.text:
# Step File / function LLM? 9 Final classification classification.py classify_cluster() Yes (conditional) 10 Significance scoring scoring.py score_cluster() No (deterministic) 11 Impact assessment impact.py build_impact_assessment() Yes (primary) 12 DetectedChange upsert inline No 13 Delivery preparation delivery_router.py prepare_delivery() No 14 Profile patch + narrative profile_updates.py Yes (narrative only) 15 Historical index historical_index.py No

Classification runs _rules_classify first (majority vote) and only calls the final_classifier LLM when the category is None, confidence < 0.6, or there are more than two candidates. Scoring is fully deterministic (see Scoring & Impact) and its band decides the DetectedChange status: Archive → archived, otherwise ready. Impact assessment is the only step that consumes the cumulative CompetitorProfile plus recent-change history, producing trend-aware GCP-specific analysis. Delivery preparation emits an AlertCandidate and/or DigestEntryDraft by band (High → both; Medium → digest, alert only if threat_level == "direct"; Low → digest only if enabled; Archive → nothing). The profile patch is applied immediately so later clusters in the same run see the updated profile.

reasoning.py record_trace() writes ReasoningTrace audit rows at intake, evidence, normalization, quality routing, clustering, classification, scoring, and detected-change build.

docs.title: A single signal's journey
docs.text:
The sequence below traces one signal, showing that the LLM is only touched when a step's deterministic pass is insufficient.

sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Orchestrator
  participant IN as intake
  participant EV as evidence
  participant NM as normalization
  participant LLM as LLMProvider
  participant QR as quality_router
  participant CLU as clustering
  participant CLS as classification
  participant SC as scoring
  participant IMP as impact
  participant DB as DB
  O->>IN: validate_candidate
  IN-->>O: valid
  O->>EV: build_evidence_bundle
  O->>NM: normalize_signal
  alt needs_llm
    NM->>LLM: signal_normalizer
    LLM-->>NM: normalized fields
  end
  O->>QR: route_signal
  QR-->>O: promote
  O->>CLU: find_or_create_cluster
  alt borderline match
    CLU->>LLM: event_merge_judge
    LLM-->>CLU: same_event?
  end
  O->>CLS: classify_cluster
  alt low confidence
    CLS->>LLM: final_classifier
  end
  O->>SC: score_cluster
  O->>IMP: build_impact_assessment
  IMP->>LLM: impact_analysis (v2, GCP)
  LLM-->>IMP: headline, so_what, threat_level
  O->>DB: upsert DetectedChange + commit

docs.title: Deduplication and clustering
docs.text: Clustering is two-tier deterministic-first. build_fingerprint() normalizes the entity (stripping suffixes like ltd/pvt/inc), slugs the action and category, and buckets the date monthly to produce a stable event_fingerprint (generic entities get a signal-scoped hash suffix). find_or_create_cluster() then tries: (1) exact fingerprint match on (competitor_id, event_fingerprint); (2) deterministic fuzzy match over the 50 most-recent non-archived clusters (same action, ≥2 shared entity words, within ±14 days, compatible category); (3) the event_merge_judge LLM for ties, which merges only when same_event is true and confidence ≥ 0.7 (conservative). DetectedChange is upserted per cluster.

docs.title: LLM usage in the pipeline
docs.text:
Step Prompt / version Output Normalization (4) signal_normalizer v1 event action, claim status, normalized summary, confidence Clustering (8) event_merge_judge v1 same_event, reason, confidence Classification (9) final_classifier v1 final category, confidence, reason Impact (11) impact_analysis v2 headline, summary, so_what, recommended_action, threat_level, watchpoints, affected GCP categories/markets Profile narrative (14) profile_narrative v1 3–4 sentence executive narrative

The impact_analysis system prompt hardcodes GCP identity, brand/category/market lists, 15 grounding rules, and an exact output-key contract. See LLM Abstraction for the full catalog.
