docs.title: Incident Response
docs.text:
This page describes the built-in incident and maintenance-action workflow used to coordinate response when the pipeline degrades or fails. It covers opening an incident, proposing and approving maintenance actions, working with Copilot-suggested actions, resolving, and reviewing afterward. All of this lives on the Incidents and Copilot observability screens and the /admin/observability/* API.

For the day-to-day watching that precedes an incident, see Monitoring & Cost.

docs.title: Create an incident
docs.text:
Open an incident when a problem needs tracking and coordination (repeated failed runs, a source that keeps erroring, a cost spike).

POST /admin/observability/incidents
{
  "title": "News scans failing for HUL",
  "severity": "sev2",
  "description": "Tavily returning 5xx; news_search jobs dead-lettering",
  "component": "layer1:news_search",
  "affected_competitors": ["<competitor-id>"],
  "affected_sources": ["<source-id>"],
  "scan_run_id": "<scan-run-id>",
  "created_by": "operator"
}
  • Severity defaults to sev2; set it to reflect blast radius (a single flaky source vs. the whole pipeline down).
  • Component identifies the failing area — align it with a stage where possible (e.g. layer1:news_search, layer2:classification).
  • Blast radius is captured through affected_competitors / affected_sources and can be refined later via PATCH.

Update an incident with PATCH /admin/observability/incidents/{id} to change status, severity, root_cause, blast_radius, component, or description as the investigation progresses.

docs.title: Maintenance actions and their approval lifecycle
docs.text:
A MaintenanceAction is a discrete remediation step attached to an incident. Actions move through an explicit approval lifecycle so risky changes are never applied without a human.

POST /admin/observability/maintenance-actions
{
  "action_type": "requeue_failed_sources",
  "description": "Re-enqueue failed news_search jobs for scan run X",
  "incident_id": "<incident-id>",
  "parameters": { "scan_run_id": "<scan-run-id>" },
  "risk_level": "medium",
  "auto_executable": false,
  "requested_by": "operator"
}

Lifecycle:

pending_approval  ──approve──►  approved  ──execute──►  executed
  • A new action starts as pending_approval.
  • PATCH /admin/observability/maintenance-actions/{id} with status=approved records approved_by.
  • PATCH ... status=executed records executed_at and stores the outcome in result_json.

Warning

Approval and execution are deliberate, human-gated steps. Do not treat approved as done — an action only takes effect when it reaches executed.

docs.title: Copilot-suggested actions (safe vs risky)
docs.text:
The Copilot assistant (POST /admin/observability/copilot) reviews live context — system health, recent runs, the last 6 hours of LLM metrics, problem sources, and open incidents — and can propose maintenance actions. It auto-creates MaintenanceAction rows with the risk gate applied automatically:

  • Safe actions are created already approved (ready to execute).
  • Risky actions are created as pending_approval, awaiting a human decision.

Note

Copilot runs on the configured LLM provider (build_llm_provider().complete_json). With the mock provider its suggestions are deterministic fixtures. Always review a risky action before approving it — Copilot proposes, humans dispose.

docs.title: Resolving
docs.text:
Resolve an incident by setting its status to resolved:

PATCH /admin/observability/incidents/{id}
{ "status": "resolved", "root_cause": "Upstream Tavily outage; recovered after retry" }

When an incident transitions to resolved, resolved_at is set automatically — you do not set the timestamp yourself. Record the root_cause and any blast_radius details in the same PATCH so the record is complete.

docs.title: Post-incident review
docs.text:
After resolution, use the incident record and its linked actions as the review artifact:

  • Read the incident's root_cause, blast_radius, and the timeline of MaintenanceAction rows (GET /admin/observability/maintenance-actions?incident_id=<id>) to reconstruct what happened and what was done.
  • Cross-reference the run that triggered it via scan_run_id and the timeline/Gantt.
  • Capture follow-ups (a permanent fix, a monitoring gap, a config change) and, where appropriate, feed them back into Troubleshooting or the Configuration reference.

docs.text:

  • Troubleshooting — symptom-to-fix guide for the common failure modes behind incidents.
  • Observability Screens — the Incidents and Copilot screens in the panel.

docs.title: Monitoring & Cost
docs.text:
This page is the operator's guide to keeping the pipeline healthy in production: what to watch day to day, how to read LLM cost, how to follow a live run, and how to get alerted when things break. Everything here is surfaced through the admin panel's Observability screens and the /admin/observability/* API, both backed by app/observability/health_aggregator.py and the telemetry model.

For the underlying telemetry model (how these numbers are produced), see Observability & Telemetry.

docs.title: What to watch
docs.text:
Three signals cover most operational health:

  • System & source health — GET /admin/observability/system-health and GET /admin/observability/source-health. Source health surfaces per-source last-scan status and lets you filter by status and competitor to find sources that are consistently failing or going stale. Use the Obs Health and Sources screens.
  • Pipeline board — GET /admin/observability/pipeline-board. Aggregates AgentRunTelemetry into per-stage stats and per-competitor stage_statuses. This is what the Live Run flowchart renders. It tells you which stage a run is in and whether any stage is failing.
  • Agent load (p95) — GET /admin/observability/agents/load?hours=24. Per-agent run count, latency (including p95, computed in Python), error rate / success rate, cost, and which agents are active right now. This is the Agent Load screen — the fastest way to spot an agent that has slowed down or started erroring.

Danger

The pipeline board keys per-competitor statuses as workflow:stage (e.g. layer2:classification) and the per-stage rollups as workflow:stage:agent_name. The panel JavaScript depends on this exact format. Never change the workflow:stage key format — it will silently break the Live Run and board screens.

docs.title: Cost tracking
docs.text:
LLM spend is tracked per call and rolled up through the telemetry hierarchy, so you can attribute cost to a run, competitor, agent, or source.

  • Cost explorer — GET /admin/observability/costs?group_by=agent|competitor|run|source&hours=24 (the Costs screen). Groups the LLMCostLedger by the chosen dimension. An invalid group_by returns 400.
  • LLM metrics & per-run cost — GET /admin/observability/llm-metrics?hours=24 and GET /admin/observability/llm-runs?hours=720. llm-runs reports cost per PipelineRun, preferring the LLMCostLedger and falling back to LLMTrace (the response's data_source field tells you which was used).
  • Ledger roll-up. Every LLM call writes one LLMCostLedger row. telemetry._propagate_cost_to_parent rolls cost up: LLMCostLedger → AgentRunTelemetry → CompetitorRun → PipelineRun. Prices come from the active LLMPriceCatalog (seeded at startup; fallback 0.005/0.015 per 1k tokens).
  • Currency. All cost figures are reported in both USD and INR, using a fixed conversion rate of USD_TO_INR = 85.

Note

If costs read as zero when using the mock provider, that is expected — MockLLMProvider reports fixed token usage and no real spend. Real cost only accrues with LLM_PROVIDER=azure_openai.

docs.title: Live run & timeline
docs.text:
To watch a run as it happens:

  • Live Run screen (loadLiveRun) polls GET /admin/observability/pipeline-board and GET /admin/observability/runs/current. runs/current returns the CurrentRunState: active stage/agent/competitor, progress percent, elapsed time, sources/signals done vs total, accumulated cost, and the list of active agents. A LIVE badge shows while a run is in progress.
  • Timeline / Gantt — GET /admin/observability/runs/{id}/timeline returns AgentRunTelemetry ordered by started_at plus a per-competitor summary, rendered as a Gantt chart on the Runs screen. Click a bar to drill into an individual agent run's inputs, outputs, duration, LLM calls, and cost.

docs.title: Alerting on failures & incidents
docs.text:
• Pipeline run status. A PipelineRun finishes as completed, degraded, or failed. Watch for degraded/failed on the Runs screen, then drill into GET /admin/observability/pipeline-runs/{id} for the per-SourceScanLog detail (error types and messages).
  • Failed jobs. GET /admin/runs/{id}/jobs lists each SourceScanLog with status, error_type, error_message, and attempt_count — the starting point for recovering a failed run.
  • Incidents. When something needs tracking and coordination, open an incident (POST /admin/observability/incidents) with a severity and affected component. See Incident Response for the full lifecycle.

docs.title: Copilot for ops
docs.text:
The Copilot screen (POST /admin/observability/copilot) is an LLM-backed operations assistant. It is given live context — system health, recent runs, the last 6 hours of LLM metrics, problem sources, and open incidents — and can propose remediation. Suggested actions are auto-created as MaintenanceAction rows: safe actions land as approved, risky ones as pending_approval awaiting a human. See Incident Response for how those actions are reviewed and executed.

Note

Copilot uses the configured LLM provider via build_llm_provider().complete_json. With the mock provider its suggestions are deterministic fixtures, not real reasoning — treat Copilot as an operator aid, not an autonomous actor.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page is a symptom-driven runbook for the most common failure modes. Each entry follows a symptom → cause → fix structure. For deeper recovery of a specific failed run, see Recover a Failed Run; for error semantics, see Error Handling, Retries & Status Codes.

docs.title: No signals produced
docs.text:
Symptom: A scan completes successfully but list-candidate-signals (or the Signals screen) is empty.

Cause: Two common reasons:

  1. First scan is a baseline. Every analyzer's first pass over a source emits only a baseline_created delta and no candidate signals — there is no previous state to diff against. Signals appear on the second and later scans, once there is something to compare.
  2. Mock provider produces limited output. With LLM_PROVIDER=mock and NEWS_PROVIDER=mock, adapters and analyzers return deterministic fixtures, not live content. Real signals require real providers.

Fix: Run the scan a second time so there is a baseline to diff against. If you need real intelligence, switch to real providers (LLM_PROVIDER=azure_openai, NEWS_PROVIDER=tavily + TAVILY_API_KEY) — see Configuration.

docs.title: Jobs not running (stuck as pending/enqueued)
docs.text:
Symptom: You submit a scan request (or run schedule-once), it returns success, but jobs never move past pending and no results appear.

Cause: In server mode nothing consumes the queue. The FastAPI server and admin scan-requests only enqueue jobs. The server-side scheduler starts only the WeeklyDigestScheduler, not a scan worker.

Fix: Run a worker to drain the queue:

ci-agent worker-once      # process the enqueued jobs
# or the all-in-one local run:
ci-agent dev-run-once     # schedule + fetch + analyze

In production, ensure a separate Service Bus consumer process is running. See Deployment → The worker in production.

Warning

This is the single most common "nothing is happening" cause. If a run sits idle, first confirm a worker/consumer is actually running.

docs.title: LLM errors (content filter, truncation, empty output)
docs.text:
Symptom: A step ran but produced no useful result; a DetectedChange has an empty impact assessment, or an LLMTrace shows an error_message.

Cause: The LLM call hit a content_filter block or was truncated by the length limit, or returned non-JSON. The provider is designed to never crash the pipeline — on any of these it returns an LLMResult with an error_message and an empty output_json (non-JSON responses are captured as {"raw_text": ...}).

Fix: Inspect the LLMTrace / LLMCostLedger for the affected step (LLM screen or GET /admin/observability/llm-runs). For truncation on the large steps (impact_analysis, competitor_query, maintenance_copilot, final_classifier), note they already use max_completion_tokens=4096; other prompts use 1024. For content-filter blocks, adjust the input payload or re-run. The pipeline continues regardless — downstream steps fall back (for example, _fallback_impact when impact LLM output is absent).

Info

Empty output_json with a populated error_message is expected, non-fatal behavior — not a crash. Treat it as a data-quality signal for that one item, not a pipeline outage.

docs.title: Duplicate competitors
docs.text:
Symptom: After loading config more than once, the same competitor (and its sources) appears multiple times.

Cause: load-config (app/admin/yaml_loader.py) always inserts — there is no upsert or dedup. Re-running it against the same YAML creates duplicate Competitor and Source rows.

Fix: Load config only once per environment. To fix existing duplicates, soft-delete the extras via the Admin Control Plane (DELETE /admin/competitors/{id}) or the panel. When iterating on config, prefer editing existing competitors/sources through the API/panel rather than reloading the YAML. See Add a Competitor & Sources.

docs.title: Schema errors
docs.text:
Symptom: Errors like "no such column" or "no such table" after pulling changes or upgrading.

Cause: The local database predates a model change. Schema is managed mostly by create_all + _safe_add_columns (Alembic is only partially adopted).

Fix:

ci-agent init-db            # create_all + _safe_add_columns
# or, if using Alembic:
alembic upgrade head
# or both together:
ci-agent init-db --alembic

See Backup & Migrations for the full picture.

docs.title: Email not sending
docs.text:
Symptom: Digest assembly succeeds and creates a WeeklyDigest, but no email arrives; delivery logs show the send was skipped.

Cause: SMTP_HOST is unset. EmailDelivery intentionally skips sending (status skipped, logged to DeliveryLog) when SMTP_HOST is empty.

Fix: Set the SMTP settings: SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT (465 uses SSL, otherwise STARTTLS), SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_FROM_EMAIL, and DEFAULT_RECIPIENTS. Then re-send. See Assemble & Send a Weekly Digest.

Info

The email client builds a permissive SSL context (check_hostname=False, CERT_NONE) on purpose, for the corporate proxy environment. This is deliberate — do not "fix" it.

docs.title: Panel data missing
docs.text:
Symptom: The Live Run flowchart or pipeline board shows no data, or stages are blank, even though runs exist.

Cause: Usually one of:

  1. Stage-key format was changed. The pipeline board keys per-competitor statuses as workflow:stage (e.g. layer2:classification) and per-stage rollups as workflow:stage:agent_name. The stage comes from AgentRunTelemetry.stage, not agent_name. The panel JS depends on this exact format — a change breaks rendering.
  2. No telemetry rows. If runs executed outside observe_agent (or the DB session factory was not wired), there are no AgentRunTelemetry rows to aggregate.

Fix: Do not change the workflow:stage key format. Confirm runs are producing AgentRunTelemetry rows (LLM/Runs screens or GET /admin/observability/pipeline-board). Confirm the correct pipeline_run_id / scan_run_id is selected.

Danger

Never change the workflow:stage key format. It is load-bearing for the admin panel JavaScript and there is no fallback.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The ci-agent command-line interface is a Typer application defined in app/cli.py. It is the primary way to run scans, drive the Layer 2 pipeline, submit feedback, tune scoring, and deliver digests outside the web admin panel. Every command below is listed with its exact name, purpose, key flags, and an example invocation.

docs.title: Invocation
docs.text:
The console entry point ci-agent (declared in pyproject.toml as ci-agent = "app.cli:app") is exactly equivalent to python -m app.cli. Both forms accept the same commands and flags:

ci-agent <command> [OPTIONS]
python -m app.cli <command> [OPTIONS]   # identical

Command names use hyphens (Typer converts the underscored function names, e.g. init_db → init-db). Run ci-agent --help for the generated catalog, or ci-agent <command> --help for a command's flags.

Note

Most commands open their own database session against DATABASE_URL and close it on exit. The server does not need to be running for CLI commands to work — they operate directly on the database and infrastructure factories.

docs.title: Setup & database
docs.text:
Command Purpose Key flags Example init-db Initialize the schema. Default runs Base.metadata.create_all plus _safe_add_columns; --alembic runs alembic upgrade head instead. --alembic ci-agent init-db load-config Load competitors and sources from a YAML config file via app/admin/yaml_loader.py. CONFIG_PATH (positional, required) ci-agent load-config examples/config/godrej_competitors.yaml

Warning

load-config always inserts — it performs no upsert or de-duplication. Re-running it on the same YAML creates duplicate competitors and sources.

docs.title: Layer 1 — scanning & inspection
docs.text:
Command Purpose Key flags Example schedule-once Enqueue all due active sources into the queue (creates a ScanRun, does not process). — ci-agent schedule-once worker-once Schedule due sources, then drain the queue with SourceScanWorker.run_until_empty(). — ci-agent worker-once dev-run-once Canonical local run: schedule + worker + printed summary table (artifacts, docs, items, deltas, packages, signals, LLM calls) for the scan run. — ci-agent dev-run-once status Show what is stored per competitor/source (items, artifacts, last scan). — ci-agent status list-scan-runs List recent scan runs with status and counts. --limit (default 10) ci-agent list-scan-runs --limit 20 list-candidate-signals List recent CandidateSignal rows (Layer 1 output). --limit (30), --verbose/-v, --status, --type ci-agent list-candidate-signals -v --status candidate show-signal Show full detail for one signal including its ChangePackage, evidence, and LLM trace. SIGNAL_ID (positional, required) ci-agent show-signal <signal-id> list-change-packages List recent ChangePackage rows with gate decisions. limit (default 20) ci-agent list-change-packages 50 export-signals-json Export candidate signals to a JSON file. --output/-o (default data/signals.json), --limit (200) ci-agent export-signals-json -o out.json export-signals Export candidate signals to a self-contained HTML report. --output/-o (default data/signals_report.html), --limit (200) ci-agent export-signals

Note

In server mode nothing consumes the queue automatically. schedule-once only enqueues; you must run worker-once (or dev-run-once, or a production Service Bus consumer) for jobs to execute. The first scan of any source produces a baseline only and emits no signals.

docs.title: Layer 2 — intelligence pipeline & inspection
docs.text: Command Purpose Key flags Example process-layer2 Run the Layer 2 pipeline over unprocessed candidate signals; prints a run-result counter summary. --scan-run-id, --candidate-signal-id, --limit (100) ci-agent process-layer2 --limit 50 layer2-dev-run Dev convenience: run the pipeline, then print the resulting detected changes. --limit (100) ci-agent layer2-dev-run run-pipeline Convenience: optionally load-config, then run a full Layer 1 scan, then Layer 2. --config, --limit (100) ci-agent run-pipeline --config examples/config/godrej_competitors.yaml list-event-clusters List EventCluster rows (competitor, category, action, status). limit (default 50) ci-agent list-event-clusters list-detected-changes List DetectedChange rows (competitor, significance, category, title). limit (default 50) ci-agent list-detected-changes list-alert-candidates List AlertCandidate rows queued for dispatch. limit (default 50) ci-agent list-alert-candidates list-digest-entry-drafts List DigestEntryDraft rows prepared for the weekly digest. limit (default 50) ci-agent list-digest-entry-drafts export-report Generate an HTML intelligence report from detected changes (via scripts/export_html_report.py). --out (default data/intelligence_report.html) ci-agent export-report --out report.html

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text:
Command Purpose Key flags Example feedback-submit Record analyst feedback on a change, cluster, or signal (does not apply side-effects). one of --change-id / --cluster-id / --signal-id; --verdict (required); --reason; --analyst (default analyst) ci-agent feedback-submit --change-id <id> --verdict false_positive feedback-list List analyst feedback entries. --unapplied, --limit (50) ci-agent feedback-list --unapplied feedback-apply Apply feedback side-effects (archive false positives, reset for reanalysis, create suppressions). --id or --all ci-agent feedback-apply --all feedback-suppressions List active Layer 1 FeedbackSuppressionEntry rules. --limit (100) ci-agent feedback-suppressions feedback-stats Show governance statistics (feedback, patterns, proposals, active rules/packs). — ci-agent feedback-stats compile-policies Compile active policy rules into a CompiledPolicyPack for an agent. AGENT_NAME (positional, required); PACK_NAME (positional, default default) ci-agent compile-policies impact_analysis

Note

feedback-submit and feedback-apply are two steps: submit records the verdict; apply executes the side-effects. Verdicts accepted by the CLI include correct, false_positive, low_priority, and needs_reanalysis. See Feedback & Learning Governance.

docs.title: Scoring weights
docs.text: Command Purpose Key flags Example scoring-weights-list List all ScoringWeightProfile entries. — ci-agent scoring-weights-list scoring-weights-create Create a profile seeded with current defaults. --name (default default), --activate/--no-activate (default activate) ci-agent scoring-weights-create --name tuned scoring-weights-show Print the currently active weights as a table. — ci-agent scoring-weights-show scoring-weights-activate Activate a profile by ID (deactivates any other active one). PROFILE_ID (positional, required) ci-agent scoring-weights-activate <id> scoring-weights-adjust Adjust one category weight by an integer delta (clamped 0–100). --profile-id, --key, --delta (all required); --reason ci-agent scoring-weights-adjust --profile-id <id> --key "Product Launch" --delta 5

docs.title: Agent configuration
docs.text: Command Purpose Key flags Example agent-config-list List all per-agent feedback configurations. — ci-agent agent-config-list agent-config-feedback Submit an instruction/correction/example/constraint to a pipeline agent. --agent, --type, --text (all required); --by (default admin) ci-agent agent-config-feedback --agent impact_analysis --type instruction --text "..." agent-config-show Show full config and feedback notes for one agent. --agent (required) ci-agent agent-config-show --agent impact_analysis agent-config-reset Clear the prompt addendum and feedback notes for an agent. --agent (required) ci-agent agent-config-reset --agent impact_analysis

docs.title: Query & delivery
docs.text:
Command Purpose Key flags Example query-profile Natural-language Q&A over a competitor's profile and recent changes (LLM). --competitor/-c, --question/-q (required); --max-changes (10) ci-agent query-profile -c "HUL" -q "What is their pricing strategy?" digest-assemble Assemble the weekly digest from ready detected changes; persists a draft WeeklyDigest. --week (ISO label, e.g. 2026-W24; defaults to current) ci-agent digest-assemble digest-list List recent weekly digests. --limit (10) ci-agent digest-list digest-send Send a digest via email. --digest-id, --to (comma-separated, both required) ci-agent digest-send --digest-id <id> --to a@x.com,b@x.com digest-preview Print a digest's HTML (or plain-text) body to stdout. --digest-id (required); --plain ci-agent digest-preview --digest-id <id> --plain pipeline-health Print a summary of pipeline health and recent feedback. — ci-agent pipeline-health

Note

Email is skipped (status skipped) if SMTP_HOST is unset; Teams alerts are skipped if TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL is unset. See Configuration & Environment.

docs.title: Configuration & Environment
docs.text: All runtime configuration lives in a single pydantic-settings Settings class (app/core/config.py). Values come from environment variables and an optional .env file, with sensible defaults baked in so the app runs offline in mock mode with no keys. This page lists every setting, grouped by subsystem, with its default and a placeholder example.

docs.title: How configuration resolves
docs.text:
1. .env is resolved relative to the project root, not the working directory. The path is computed in code as Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / ".env", so ci-agent and uvicorn pick up the same .env regardless of where you launch them.
  2. Settings is a singleton. get_settings() builds the Settings object once and caches it in a module global; every caller shares the same instance for the process lifetime.
  3. Unknown keys are ignored. Settings.Config sets extra = "ignore", so .env.example may be a subset and extra environment variables do not raise.
  4. Per-source YAML config overrides .env. Where a source's config_json block (from the competitor YAML) sets an option that also exists as an environment default — e.g. a news provider, query_budget, or bing_market — the per-source YAML value takes precedence for that source. Environment settings are the fallback.

Danger

Never print or commit real secrets. .env is gitignored and holds real API keys; .env.example is the safe, placeholder-only template. All examples on this page use placeholders such as <key> and https://<your-resource>.openai.azure.com. The local database (data/*.db) and blob store hold real competitor data and are never committed.

docs.title: Permissive SSL is deliberate
docs.text:
Info

All outbound adapter HTTP uses httpx with verify=False, and the email delivery path builds a permissive SSL context (check_hostname=False, CERT_NONE). This is an intentional accommodation for the corporate proxy environment — do not "fix" it by enabling verification. It is a known, load-bearing setting, not an oversight.

docs.title: Data Model & Enums
docs.text: Every persistent entity is a SQLAlchemy model in app/db/models.py, grouped below by subsystem. This page is a dry, table-by-table inventory of the models and their key columns plus the shared enum values. For how these entities relate and flow into one another — the lineage chain and the entity-relationship diagram — see Data model & lineage.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Primary keys are UUID strings (String columns defaulting to str(uuid.uuid4())), not integers.
  • JSON columns carry the _json suffix (e.g. aliases_json, evidence_json, weights_json, metadata_json) and hold lists or dicts.
  • Timestamps are naive UTC (created_at, updated_at, plus per-entity *_at columns).
  • All database access flows through app/db/repositories.py. Routes and workers call repository functions rather than issuing raw ORM queries; the CLI inspection commands are the only routine exception.
  • Status columns are plain strings validated against the enums documented at the end of this page.

docs.title: Error Handling, Retries & Status Codes
docs.text: This page documents how the system behaves when things fail: how the Layer 1 worker fails and retries jobs, how LLM calls degrade without crashing, which HTTP status codes the admin API returns, how orphaned runs are reclaimed on startup, and the common error_type values you will see in the logs. It is a reference companion to Recover a Failed Run.

docs.title: Worker error paths
docs.text:
The Layer 1 worker (app/workers/source_scan_worker.py, SourceScanWorker.process_job) distinguishes two failure classes, which behave asymmetrically on the queue:

  • Pre-flight failures (before the adapter runs) — e.g. the adapter or analyzer for a source_type cannot be resolved. These call _fail_job, which marks the SourceScanLog failed and calls queue.retry. The queue increments the job's attempt count and re-delivers it, dead-lettering after MAX_QUEUE_ATTEMPTS (default 3).
  • Runtime failures (during adapter or analyzer execution) — an exception thrown while fetching or analyzing. These mark the log failed, update scan timestamps to failed, and queue.ack the job (no retry).

Warning

This ack-vs-retry asymmetry is deliberate but easy to misread: a missing adapter/analyzer registration is retried and eventually dead-lettered, whereas an exception inside a working adapter is acknowledged and not retried. A source that fails at runtime will not re-run on its own — re-drive it with a retry_failed scan request or the next scheduled scan.

A missing source/competitor is a terminal case: the log is marked failed with a not-found error, the job is acked, and process_job returns False.

docs.title: Dead-lettering
docs.text: The queue (InMemorySourceScanQueue locally, AzureServiceBusSourceScanQueue in production) increments attempt on each retry and moves the job to the dead-letter path once attempt exceeds MAX_QUEUE_ATTEMPTS. Tune the threshold with the MAX_QUEUE_ATTEMPTS setting — see Configuration & Environment.

docs.title: LLM failure semantics
docs.text:
Warning

LLM failures never crash the pipeline. The provider (AzureOpenAIProvider) wraps every call in try/except and always returns an LLMResult — it never raises.

On failure or degradation the provider returns an LLMResult with:

  • error_message set (populated for content-filter blocks and length-truncation cases), and
  • output_json empty ({}); non-JSON model output is returned as {"raw_text": ...}.

Because analyzers and the Layer 2 orchestrator treat an empty output_json as "no LLM contribution," a failed LLM call degrades gracefully to the deterministic path rather than aborting the run. Each call is still recorded as an LLMTrace (with the error_message) and a cost-ledger row. See LLM Abstraction.

docs.title: HTTP status codes
docs.text:
The admin API (all routers under app/admin/) uses conventional REST status codes. Error bodies follow the Error("<status>: <text>") convention.

Code Meaning Typical endpoints 200 Success (reads, updates). Most GET/PATCH/PUT endpoints. 201 Created. POST /admin/competitors, .../sources, POST /admin/scan-runs, schedule/news-profile create, POST /admin/incidents, proposal/eval/pack creation. 202 Accepted — work runs in the background. POST /admin/scan-requests (dispatches _run_scan_in_background). 204 No content — soft delete. DELETE /admin/competitors/{id}, .../sources/{id}, .../schedule, news-profile delete. 400 Bad request. e.g. GET /admin/observability/costs with an invalid group_by. 404 Not found. GET /admin/competitors/{id}, .../scan-runs/{id}, .../runs/{id}, schedule/news-profile/coverage-map lookups, etc. 409 Conflict — resource already exists. POST /admin/sources/{id}/schedule when a schedule exists; news-profile create when one exists. 422 Unprocessable — invalid enum/payload. POST /admin/detected-changes/{id}/feedback with an invalid verdict.

Note

POST /admin/scan-requests returns 202, not 201: it enqueues work and returns immediately. In server mode nothing consumes the queue automatically, so a 202 means "accepted and enqueued," not "executed." A worker or Service Bus consumer must run for the jobs to complete.

docs.title: Orphan / interrupted marking on startup
docs.text:
On application startup (app/main.py) the app marks any PipelineRun, ScanRun, and AgentRunTelemetry rows still in a running state as interrupted. This reclaims runs left dangling by a crash or an abrupt shutdown so the observability views do not show perpetually "running" work. (Startup uses the deprecated on_event hook rather than the newer lifespan API.)

The scan-run cleanup endpoint POST /admin/scan-runs/cleanup performs a related manual reclamation, transitioning stuck running scan runs so they no longer block the console.

docs.title: Common error_type values
docs.text:
SourceScanLog.error_type and error_message capture the failure reason for a source scan. Common error_type values include:

  • NotFound — the source or competitor could not be loaded.
  • Adapter/analyzer resolution failures — no adapter or analyzer registered for the source_type.
  • Adapter runtime exceptions — network/parse errors raised during fetch (surfaced with the exception text in error_message).
  • Analyzer runtime exceptions — errors raised during analysis.

Inspect these per job via GET /admin/runs/{id}/jobs (each row resolves source_name, status, attempt_count, error_type, error_message) or with ci-agent list-scan-runs and the panel's Runs screen.

docs.title: API — Competitors, Sources, Runs & Audit
docs.text:
This page is the endpoint reference for the core admin router (app/admin/routes.py) and the scan-request router (app/admin/scan_request_routes.py). It covers the health check, competitor and source CRUD, scan-run management, background scan requests, run visibility, and the audit log. Request and response schemas are defined in app/schemas/admin.py.

No authentication

These endpoints have no auth layer — do not expose them to an untrusted network. The changed_by / requested_by / role fields are caller-supplied strings, not verified identities.

docs.title: Scan Requests
docs.text:
A ScanRequest is the high-level, background-executed trigger for a scan. POST returns immediately with 202; the work runs in a background task (_run_scan_in_background) which updates the request status as it progresses. Status transitions: created → running → completed / failed.

The six request_type values and their params_json shapes (see How-to: Run a Manual Scan):

request_type params_json Behavior all_sources {} Enqueue all due sources (schedule_scan with no filter). competitor_sources { "competitor_id": "…" } Enqueue all active sources for the competitor. Fails if competitor_id missing. single_source { "source_id": "…" } Enqueue one source. Fails if source_id missing. layer2_only { "scan_run_id"?: "…", "competitor_id"?: "…", "limit"?: int } Run the Layer 2 orchestrator only; skips the queue. All keys optional. retry_failed { "scan_run_id": "…" } Re-enqueue SourceScanLog rows with status="failed" for that run. rebaseline { "source_id": "…" } Clear the source's last_scan_at, then enqueue it.

docs.title: POST /admin/scan-requests
docs.text:
Submit a scan request; executes asynchronously in a background thread. Also writes an AdminAuditLog entry (action="trigger_scan", capturing the request payload and caller IP). Component: Control plane. Backing code: app/admin/scan_request_routes.py → create_scan_request().

Request body — schema ScanRequestCreate (app/schemas/admin.py)

Field Type Required Default Description request_type enum all_sources\|competitor_sources\|single_source\|layer2_only\|retry_failed\|rebaseline yes — Which scan action to run. params_json object no {} Parameters for the chosen request_type (see table above). requested_by string no "admin" Caller label (unverified). role string | null no null Caller role label (unverified). 
// Example request body
{
  "request_type": "competitor_sources",
  "params_json": { "competitor_id": "9f3c1e28-…" },
  "requested_by": "krishna",
  "role": "analyst"
}

Response — 202 Accepted → ScanRequestOut (initial state; status is created, scan_run_id still null)

Field Type Description id string (UUID) Scan request id. request_type string The submitted request type. params_json object The submitted params. status string created → running → completed/failed. requested_by string Caller label. role string | null Caller role. scan_run_id string (UUID) | null Set once the background task creates/links a run; null for layer2_only and until then. sources_enqueued int Number of sources enqueued (populated on completion). error_message string | null Failure reason (null unless status="failed"; truncated to 500 chars). created_at datetime (ISO 8601) Creation timestamp. updated_at datetime (ISO 8601) Last status update timestamp. 
// Example 202 response
{
  "id": "e1f2a3b4-…",
  "request_type": "competitor_sources",
  "params_json": { "competitor_id": "9f3c1e28-…" },
  "status": "created",
  "requested_by": "krishna",
  "role": "analyst",
  "scan_run_id": null,
  "sources_enqueued": 0,
  "error_message": null,
  "created_at": "2026-07-08T05:00:00+00:00",
  "updated_at": "2026-07-08T05:00:00+00:00"
}

Status codes: 202 accepted (work runs in background) · 422 validation error. Per-type failures (e.g. missing source_id, queue not initialised) are not HTTP errors — they surface as status="failed" + error_message on a later GET.

docs.title: API — Feedback Governance & Policy Health
docs.text:
This page documents the governance endpoints of the intelligence router (app/admin/intelligence_routes.py, all under /admin/feedback/*) and the policy-health router (app/admin/policy_health_routes.py, under /admin/policy-health/*). These endpoints drive the human-review governance lifecycle: legacy suppressions, proposals, policy packs, patterns, rules, evaluation, weight profiles, runtime state, and the policy-health snapshot/consolidation tools. See Concepts: Feedback & Learning for the model.

Every endpoint below takes and returns hand-built dict payloads — none use a Pydantic response_model, and request bodies are untyped dict (the route reads specific keys, documented per endpoint). Timestamps are ISO 8601 strings. IDs are UUID strings.

Two suppression systems, not unified

Legacy FeedbackSuppressionEntry (Layer 1, enforced in the scan worker and news analyzer) and governance SuppressionRule (Layer 2, enforced in the orchestrator) are separate tables. The /admin/feedback/suppressions endpoints below manage the legacy table; governance SuppressionRule rows are created via proposal approval or the NL command.

Governance pipeline is deterministic

Feature extraction, pattern mining, and proposal generation use no LLM. LLM is used only in the legacy weight-adjustment decision, natural-language command parsing (POST /admin/feedback/nl-command), policy consolidation (POST /admin/policy-health/{pack_id}/consolidate), and eval runs of LLM agents.

Budget constants

Defined in app/feedback/policy_compiler.py: per-pack token budget MAX_POLICY_PACK_TOKENS = 400, per-run token budget MAX_AGENT_POLICY_TOKENS_PER_RUN = 800, max MAX_RULES_PER_PACK = 8 rules per pack, max MAX_POLICY_PACKS_PER_AGENT_RUN = 5 packs per agent run, near-budget warning at 0.80 utilisation. Token estimate ≈ 1.3 tokens/word (_estimate_tokens).

docs.title: Suppressions (legacy)
docs.text: Manages FeedbackSuppressionEntry rows (Layer 1 suppressions).

docs.text:
List legacy suppression entries, newest first. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/intelligence_routes.py → list_feedback_suppressions().

Query parameters

docs.title: POST /admin/feedback/proposals/{proposal_id}/approve
docs.text:
Approve a proposal and immediately activate it. Only pending_human_review proposals are approvable. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/intelligence_routes.py → approve_proposal() → HumanReviewService.approve_proposal().

Path parameters

Name Type Description proposal_id string (UUID) Proposal to approve.

Request body — untyped dict

Field Type Required Default Description reviewer string no "admin" Recorded as reviewed_by. edited_change_json object no — If supplied, replaces proposed_change_json and sets status to edited_and_approved (otherwise approved). Activation then uses the edited payload.

Activation effect by proposal_type:

  • suppression_rule → creates one governance SuppressionRule per entry in all_values (falls back to a single value); skips values that already have an active rule.
  • scoring_weight_change → supersedes the active ScoringWeightProfile and creates a new active profile with the changed category weight.
  • agent_policy_rule → creates an active AgentPolicyRule for target_agent, then auto-recompiles that agent's default policy pack.
// Example request body (approve with an edit)
{
  "reviewer": "krishna",
  "edited_change_json": {
    "agent_name": "classifier",
    "rule_text": "Never classify distributor onboarding as Partnership / Acquisition.",
    "scope": { "category": "Partnership / Acquisition" },
    "priority": 55
  }
}

Response — 200 OK → object

Field Type Description proposal_id string (UUID) The proposal id. status string approved or edited_and_approved. activated list[object] Objects created/activated; each has type plus type-specific keys (id, value, category, agent, tokens, …). 
// Example 200 response
{
  "proposal_id": "prop-0001-4a1b-9c2d-000000000001",
  "status": "edited_and_approved",
  "activated": [
    { "type": "agent_policy_rule", "id": "rule-77a1-...-01", "agent": "classifier" },
    { "type": "compiled_policy_pack", "id": "pack-9f0c-...-02", "agent": "classifier", "tokens": 214, "auto_recompiled": true }
  ]
}

Status codes: 200 approved · 400 proposal not found, or not in pending_human_review (both surface via the error field mapped to 400).

docs.title: POST /admin/feedback/policy-packs/compile
docs.text:
Compile a new policy pack. Supersedes any active pack with the same agent_name + pack_name. Newly compiled packs start in draft (or budget_exceeded, all-active mode only) and must be activated separately. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/intelligence_routes.py → compile_policy_pack() (and PolicyCompiler.compile_pack() for all-active mode).

Request body — untyped dict. The route picks one of three modes by which key is present:

Common fields (all modes):

Field Type Required Default Description agent_name string no "unknown" Owning agent. pack_name string no "default" Pack name. scope_json object no {} Free-form scope metadata stored on the pack.

Mode-specific fields:

Field Type Mode Description custom_text string custom_text Fully hand-written pack text. When present, rule lookup is skipped; included_policy_rule_ids_json is []. Empty string → text becomes "(empty pack)". Status is always draft (no budget downgrade). rule_ids list[string (UUID)] rule_ids Explicit rule ids; compiled as a numbered list in the given order (unknown ids dropped). Status is always draft. reviewer string all-active (default) Used only when neither custom_text nor rule_ids is present. Compiles all active rules for agent_name in priority order, capped at min(settings.MAX_POLICY_RULES_PER_PACK, 8). Status becomes budget_exceeded if the estimate exceeds 400, else draft. Defaults to "admin". 

// Example request body — custom_text mode
{ "agent_name": "classifier", "pack_name": "default", "custom_text": "1. Prefer Regulatory / Legal over Product Launch when a recall is mentioned." }

// Example request body — rule_ids mode
{ "agent_name": "classifier", "pack_name": "default", "rule_ids": ["rule-77a1-...-01", "rule-77a1-...-04"] }

// Example request body — all-active mode
{ "agent_name": "classifier", "pack_name": "default", "reviewer": "krishna" }

Response — 200 OK → object (identical across all three modes)

Field Type Description id string (UUID) New pack id. version string Version label. token_estimate int Estimated tokens. status enum draft\|budget_exceeded New pack status. 
// Example 200 response
{ "id": "pack-9f0c-4a1b-9c2d-000000000010", "version": "v4", "token_estimate": 41, "status": "draft" }

Status codes: 200 compiled (no explicit 201).

{ "compiled_text": "1. Prefer Regulatory / Legal over Product Launch when a recall is mentioned.\n2. Ignore reseller listings." }

Response — 200 OK → object

Field Type Description id string (UUID) Pack id. pack_name string Current name. token_estimate int Recomputed estimate. status string Unchanged pack status. compiled_text string Current pack text. 
// Example 200 response
{
  "id": "pack-9f0c-4a1b-9c2d-000000000010",
  "pack_name": "default",
  "token_estimate": 63,
  "status": "draft",
  "compiled_text": "1. Prefer Regulatory / Legal over Product Launch when a recall is mentioned.\n2. Ignore reseller listings."
}

Status codes: 200 updated · 404 pack not found.

docs.title: POST /admin/feedback/policy-packs/{pack_id}/activate
docs.text:
Activate a draft pack after passing budget checks. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/intelligence_routes.py → activate_policy_pack() → PolicyCompiler.activate_pack().

Path parameters

Name Type Description pack_id string (UUID) Pack to activate.

Request body — untyped dict

Field Type Required Default Description reviewer string no "admin" Recorded as approved_by.

Activation is blocked (raises, mapped to 404 — see status codes) if any check fails: token estimate > 400, rule count > 8, or duplicate rules detected (first 60 chars of two rules match). On success, status becomes active, activated_at is set, and a fresh health snapshot is written.

// Example request body
{ "reviewer": "krishna" }

Response — 200 OK → object

Field Type Description id string (UUID) Pack id. status string active on success. 
// Example 200 response
{ "id": "pack-9f0c-4a1b-9c2d-000000000010", "status": "active" }

Status codes: 200 activated · 404 pack not found or activation blocked by budget/rule-count/duplicate checks (the route maps the compiler's ValueError to 404 for both cases; the error detail carries the blocking reasons).

docs.title: GET /admin/feedback/runtime-state
docs.text:
Live view of active rules, packs, weight profile, and suppressions currently in force, grouped per agent. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/intelligence_routes.py → get_runtime_state().

Response — 200 OK → object

Field Type Description agents list[object] Per-agent state (see below). weight_profile string Active profile name, or "defaults". active_suppressions int Count of active governance SuppressionRule rows. scoring_weights_preview object {category_scores: {...}} from the effective weights.

Each agents[] entry:

Field Type Description agent_name string Agent. active_rules int Number of active rules. active_packs int Number of active packs. total_pack_tokens int Summed token_estimate across active packs. rules list[object] {id, rule_text (truncated to 80 chars), scope}. packs list[object] {id, pack_name, version, token_estimate}.

When there are no active rules or packs, agents falls back to a default set: classifier, scorer, impact_analysis, relevance_filter.

// Example 200 response
{
  "agents": [
    {
      "agent_name": "classifier",
      "active_rules": 1,
      "active_packs": 1,
      "total_pack_tokens": 214,
      "rules": [ { "id": "rule-77a1-...-01", "rule_text": "Do not classify routine distributor appointments as Partnership / Acqui", "scope": { "category": "Partnership / Acquisition" } } ],
      "packs": [ { "id": "pack-9f0c-...-02", "pack_name": "default", "version": "v3", "token_estimate": 214 } ]
    }
  ],
  "weight_profile": "feedback_adjusted_pricing_change",
  "active_suppressions": 4,
  "scoring_weights_preview": { "category_scores": { "Pricing Change": 27, "Product Launch": 30 } }
}

Status codes: 200 OK.

docs.title: POST /admin/feedback/nl-command
docs.text:
Parse a free-text governance command with the LLM and execute it immediately. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/intelligence_routes.py → nl_governance_command().

Request body — untyped dict

Field Type Required Default Description command string yes — Free-text instruction. Trimmed; empty → 400. analyst string no "admin" Attribution for created rows.

The LLM parses command into one of: add_rule, suppress, adjust_weight, compile_pack, deactivate_rule, query. The route then executes:

  • add_rule → creates an active AgentPolicyRule directly (not a proposal).
  • suppress → creates an active governance SuppressionRule directly.
  • adjust_weight → supersedes the active profile and creates a new active ScoringWeightProfile with the adjusted category value (only if the category currently exists).
  • compile_pack → recompiles the agent's pack via PolicyCompiler.
  • deactivate_rule → sets matching active rules to inactive (by keyword + optional agent filter).
  • query → no side effects.

No proposal is created

Despite the parser's own requires_approval hint, all actions execute directly. proposals_created is always [].

// Example request body
{ "command": "Make the classifier stop tagging distributor appointments as partnerships", "analyst": "krishna" }

Response — 200 OK → object

Field Type Description command string Echoed command. action_type enum add_rule\|suppress\|adjust_weight\|compile_pack\|deactivate_rule\|query Parsed action. human_summary string LLM one-line summary of the action. executed list[object] Objects created/changed; each has type plus type-specific keys. proposals_created list Always empty. 
// Example 200 response
{
  "command": "Make the classifier stop tagging distributor appointments as partnerships",
  "action_type": "add_rule",
  "human_summary": "Add a classifier rule to not label distributor appointments as Partnership / Acquisition.",
  "executed": [ { "type": "agent_policy_rule", "id": "rule-77a1-...-12", "agent": "classifier" } ],
  "proposals_created": []
}

Status codes: 200 OK · 400 command missing · 500 LLM parse failed or execution failed.

docs.title: Policy Health (/admin/policy-health/*)
docs.text: Backed by app/admin/policy_health_routes.py. A pack dict (_pack_to_dict) used across these responses carries: id, agent_name, pack_name, version, status, token_estimate, token_budget (400), budget_utilization, rule_count, created_at, activated_at. docs.title: POST /admin/policy-health/{pack_id}/consolidate
docs.text:
Ask the LLM to propose a consolidation (merge / retire / convert / split) for a pack's rules, persisting a PolicyConsolidationProposal in pending_review. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/policy_health_routes.py → generate_consolidation_proposal().

Path parameters

Name Type Description pack_id string (UUID) Pack to consolidate.

No request body. The pack must have at least one included rule.

Response — 201 Created → proposal dict (_proposal_to_dict)

Field Type Description id string (UUID) Proposal id. policy_pack_id string (UUID) Target pack. agent_name string Pack's agent. proposal_type enum merge_rules\|retire_stale\|split_pack\|convert_to_hard_rule LLM-chosen consolidation type. reason string Why this consolidation. current_token_estimate int Pack tokens before. proposed_token_estimate int Estimated tokens after. expected_token_reduction int max(0, current − proposed). rules_to_merge list[string (UUID)] Rule ids to merge. rules_to_convert list[string (UUID)] Rule ids better as hard rules. rules_to_retire list[string (UUID)] Stale/redundant rule ids. proposed_compiled_text string Optimised pack text. status string Always pending_review. created_by string "admin". reviewed_by string | null Reviewer (initially null). reviewed_at datetime | null Review time (initially null). created_at datetime | null Creation timestamp. 
// Example 201 response
{
  "id": "cons-0001-...-01",
  "policy_pack_id": "pack-9f0c-...-02",
  "agent_name": "classifier",
  "proposal_type": "merge_rules",
  "reason": "Rules 2 and 5 both cover distributor news; merge into one.",
  "current_token_estimate": 214,
  "proposed_token_estimate": 150,
  "expected_token_reduction": 64,
  "rules_to_merge": ["rule-77a1-...-02", "rule-77a1-...-05"],
  "rules_to_convert": [],
  "rules_to_retire": ["rule-77a1-...-08"],
  "proposed_compiled_text": "1. Do not classify distributor appointments or renewals as Partnership / Acquisition.",
  "status": "pending_review",
  "created_by": "admin",
  "reviewed_by": null,
  "reviewed_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-07-09T09:05:00"
}

Status codes: 201 created · 400 pack has no rules to consolidate · 404 pack not found · 500 LLM consolidation failed.

docs.title: POST /admin/policy-health/simulate
docs.text:
Simulate which active packs would load for an agent run and whether the combined token budget stays within the per-run limit (800). Persists a PolicyPackSimulationResult. Component: Feedback governance. Backing code: app/admin/policy_health_routes.py → simulate_agent_run().

Request body — untyped dict

Field Type Required Default Description agent_name string yes — Agent to simulate. Empty → 400. task_context object no {} Free-form context stored on the result (not used for selection).

Selection: all active packs for the agent, newest first, capped at MAX_POLICY_PACKS_PER_AGENT_RUN (5). activation_allowed is true when the summed token_estimate of the selected packs is ≤ 800.

// Example request body
{ "agent_name": "classifier", "task_context": { "workflow": "layer2", "stage": "classification" } }

Response — 201 Created → object

Field Type Description simulation_id string (UUID) New simulation id. agent_name string Simulated agent. matching_packs list[object] Selected packs, each a pack dict (see section intro). total_available_packs int All active packs found for the agent. selected_pack_count int Packs actually selected (≤ 5). total_policy_tokens int Sum of selected packs' token estimates. token_budget int 800. activation_allowed bool true if within budget. failure_reason string | null Why activation is blocked and/or a note when more than 5 packs exist. 
// Example 201 response
{
  "simulation_id": "sim-0001-...-01",
  "agent_name": "classifier",
  "matching_packs": [
    { "id": "pack-9f0c-...-02", "agent_name": "classifier", "pack_name": "default", "version": "v3", "status": "active", "token_estimate": 214, "token_budget": 400, "budget_utilization": 0.535, "rule_count": 3, "created_at": "2026-07-06T14:05:00", "activated_at": "2026-07-06T14:07:11" }
  ],
  "total_available_packs": 1,
  "selected_pack_count": 1,
  "total_policy_tokens": 214,
  "token_budget": 800,
  "activation_allowed": true,
  "failure_reason": null
}

Status codes: 201 created · 400 agent_name missing.
